Notes:

- **LL-0042.** The statement is for a tetrahedron (n = 3): edge lengths as the hinge volumes, at a non-degenerate tetrahedron, in every direction of the six edge lengths, with the interior dihedral angles. The cited identity, eq. (8) of Dittrich, Freidel and Speziale, holds for an n-simplex; the general case, which the 4-simplex needs, is not formalized here.
- **LL-0048.** Sorkin's complex Lorentzian angles, with the complex action weighted by Z = -i on spacelike and 1 on timelike triangles. For a 4D triangulation embedded in Minkowski space, every deficit angle vanishes (IsGeometric4.lorDeficit_eq_zero), the action is differentiable in the squared edge lengths with the Lorentzian Schläfli identity (lorSchlaefli4_finset, hasFDerivAt_lorReggeAction), and the flat configuration is stationary (lorReggeAction_stationary). Euclidean angles on the same Lorentzian data give deficit π, so the Lorentzian angles are needed (wrong_eucAngle_T). Null triangles and tetrahedra are excluded (IsNonNull4); the null cases are not covered. Checked numerically (scripts/regge).
- **LL-0053.** For a Riemannian metric on a region of the plane, ρ-fat vertex stars of bounded valence with geodesic edge lengths and mesh h, and a Lipschitz weight f, |Σ_v f(v) δ_v − ∫ f K dA| ≤ C h. The angle bound of the stars is derived from fatness (Lightlike.CMS.angle_le_of_fat). The vertex cells, of area ½Σ det2 and covering the region three times outside a boundary layer of area at most b h, are hypotheses; building them from an explicit triangulation is not proven, so this is not yet the theorem of Cheeger, Müller and Schrader (Commun. Math. Phys. 92 (1984) 405), which is in every dimension. As checks, the flat metric gives density 0, the integral of the Gauss curvature of the round sphere over its chart cell is 4π (a chart integral, Lightlike.CMS.sph_integral, not a deficit sum on a triangulated sphere; the deficit sum 4π of the octahedron in the unit sphere is Lightlike.Regge.octahedron_deficit_sum), and the curvature density without the area weight gives 2π², not 4π. Non-vacuity is shown on a single flat star with four neighbours, which meets every hypothesis with an empty region Ω (the cell is its own boundary layer); a non-empty region is LL-0054's grid. The comparison with the cited source is pending. The statement differs from the Cheeger–Müller–Schrader theorem, which holds in every dimension and for arbitrary fine triangulations, in these ways, namely a planar region only (one chart), ρ-fat vertex stars of bounded valence, geodesic edge lengths, a Lipschitz weight, the rate O(h), and the vertex cells as hypotheses.
- **LL-0054.** The vertex cells of LL-0053 are built from a triangulation given by vertex positions and corner maps, not assumed. The star cell of an interior vertex is the union of its triangles, its area is ½Σ det2, and the triangles cover the interior region three times outside the triangles with a corner off V. The corners of a star triangle agree with (v, nb v j, nb v (j+1)) up to a permutation of Fin 3; the first version of the statement fixed their order, which left no triangle with all corners in V, and was corrected. The remaining hypotheses are that distinct triangles overlap in null sets, that the star of every interior vertex winds once (its angles sum to 2π), that the number of boundary triangles times h is bounded, that every triangle lies in K, and that edges at the first corner of each triangle have length at most h; the integral runs over the triangles with all three corners in V. Non-vacuity is shown on a 4×4 vertex grid with the 4 central vertices interior, valence 6 and the flat metric (Lightlike.CMS.grid_triangulation_bound), with 2 interior and 16 boundary triangles and an interior region of positive area (Lightlike.CMS.grid_interior_positive); the flat metric makes the integral 0. For a non-flat metric the n×n grids of the unit square, h = 1/n, satisfy the hypotheses with constants independent of n, so the deficit sum is within C/n of the interior integral for every large n (Lightlike.CMS.refining_grid_bound); for the metric dx² + e^{2x}dy² of scalar curvature −2 (Lightlike.CMS.scalar_hyp) that integral is at most −1/4 for every n ≥ 4 (Lightlike.CMS.hyp_refining_grid). The deficit angles there are those of the chart geodesic distances, which are not computed explicitly. As wrong-model checks, a clockwise star fails the fatness hypothesis for every ρ > 0 (Lightlike.CMS.reversed_star_not_fat), and Lightlike.CMS.volume_real_tri_example computes a triangle area of 3, not the 6 of the unhalved determinant. This is the planar case only, not the theorem of Cheeger, Müller and Schrader in every dimension.
- **LL-0056.** For a Riemannian coordinate metric g on U and a compact K ⊆ U, |d(m − Δ/2, m + Δ/2)² − g_m(Δ,Δ) − Q_m(Δ)| ≤ C‖Δ‖⁶ for m in K and small Δ, with the quartic form Q_m(Δ) = (1/24)∂_Δ∂_Δ g(Δ,Δ) − (1/12)g(Γ(Δ,Δ),Γ(Δ,Δ)); about the midpoint the terms of order three and five vanish. The order is sharp: on the cubic shear the remainder is t⁶/576 along Δ = (t, 0), so it is not O(‖Δ‖⁷) (Lightlike.Geodesic.dist_sq_expansion_midpoint6_sharp), and the expansion is checked exactly there (Lightlike.Geodesic.cubicShear_dist_sq_expansion_midpoint6). Brewin (2009), Section 9, gives the expansion in Riemann normal coordinates and the midpoint form d² = g(m)(Δ, Δ) + O(‖Δ‖⁴); the quartic form Q_m and the sixth-order bound are derived here.
- **LL-0057.** For the Riemannian bundle of g on U, Mathlib's riemannianEDist is the infimum of the lengths of admissible curves, with no hypothesis on the points (the empty infimum is ⊤). If an admissible curve joins x and y it equals ENNReal.ofReal (dist g U x y), and on a preconnected U this holds for all x, y. Without an admissible curve riemannianEDist is ⊤ while the chart distance takes the junk value 0. This connects the geodesic results of this library (LL-0045, LL-0056) to Mathlib's Riemannian distance.
- **LL-0058.** The map from the ten squared edge lengths of a 4-simplex to its ten squared triangle areas (Heron's formula in squared lengths) has invertible Jacobian at the regular simplex (all squared lengths 1; jac_regular_isUnit, through an explicit integer inverse of the edge-triangle incidence matrix), so by the inverse function theorem it is injective on a neighbourhood of the regular simplex with open image, and so are the areas themselves. The result is local: at the corner configuration (squared lengths 1 on the edges at one vertex, 2 on the others) the Jacobian is singular (jac_corner_det, with an explicit kernel vector), and corner_pair gives two different length assignments, the corner configuration moved by plus and minus half that kernel vector, both satisfying the Gram-minor criterion IsSimplex, with the same ten areas. IsSimplex is the positivity of the leading principal minors of the Gram matrix; Realization.lean gives both assignments as the squared distances of affinely independent five-point sets in ℝ⁴, so they are Euclidean 4-simplices of non-zero volume (Lightlike.AreaRegge.corner_pair_realized). scripts/regge/area_jacobian_check.py recomputes det Jac = −48/8¹⁰ at the regular simplex, the corner kernel and the corner pair in SymPy.
- **LL-0063.** For a symmetric, C³, compactly supported perturbation h of the flat metric of the plane and a C¹ compactly supported weight f, the weighted sum of the linearized vertex deficit angles of the diagonal grid of mesh 1/n differs from ∫ f · linCurv h by at most C/n, where linCurv h = ∂₀∂₁h₀₁ − ½(∂₁²h₀₀ + ∂₀²h₁₁) is the linearized Gauss curvature (linearized_regge_converges). The squared edge lengths are ∫₀¹ (δ + εh)(e, e) dt along the edge vector e, that is ℓ_e²(1 + ε ⨍_e h(t_e, t_e)), Christiansen's degrees of freedom of the Regge interpolant (eq. (5)); this is the first variation of the squared length, not the distance of the perturbed metric; tying them to that distance is open. For a quadratic perturbation the deficit is exactly s² linCurv (linDef_model), and the flat star has deficit 0. Christiansen works in dimension 3; this is the 2D analogue on one grid family, and the Regge action itself is not treated. A perturbation with a positive limit shows non-vacuity, and dropping the ∂₀∂₁h₀₁ term gives the limit 0, which the deficits do not approach. The nonlinear 2D statement, for geodesic edge lengths, is LL-0053 (after Cheeger, Müller and Schrader).
- **LL-0078.** G is any positive definite 3x3 matrix; the incidences are the 36 pairs (tetrahedron, hinge) of the Kuhn triangulation of the unit cube (six tetrahedra, seven edge directions). Each class of incidences is a fan of four or six tetrahedra around the hinge axis; the proof uses the complex coordinate in the plane quotient, so it holds for every G and does not use G = identity. Limits: only the cube star of one lattice point is treated; nothing is said about a triangulation of a manifold, and the lattice is the standard one (no other triangulations).
- **LL-0079.** For a coordinate metric g on an open set U (smooth, symmetric, invertible) and a point m of U: the derivative of the inverse metric is minus g⁻¹ (∂g) g⁻¹ (pd_inv), and the derivative of the Christoffel symbols, the Riemann tensor and the scalar curvature at m are written with (g m)⁻¹, ∂g(m) and ∂∂g(m) only. Limits: this unfolds the coordinate definitions of the library (Lightlike.christoffel, riemann, scalarCurvature); it is the textbook computation, not a statement about tensors or charts.
- **LL-0080.** Part of the 3D convergence of the Regge action (T-RC6), which stays open. Scope: at a point m where all first partial derivatives of a Riemannian metric g on an open set of R^3 vanish (for example the centre of normal coordinates); not the general chart. The convergence theorem needs the same statement at every hinge, where the first derivatives do not vanish, and that case is open. For any positive definite g(m) and any second derivatives, the star of one edge of the Kuhn triangulation (flat star: the dihedral angles of each of the seven edge classes add up to 2π; first-order coefficient 0; weights: the hinge lengths √(g(m)(w, w)) of the seven directions w, where g(m)(w, w) is the squared length) satisfies: the sum over the seven classes of the hinge length times the second-order coefficient of the class angle sum equals minus half the scalar curvature times the square root of det g(m) (JetStarCore). The core is an exact polynomial identity in the six entries of g(m) and the 36 independent second derivatives (flat_star_identity), generated and checked in exact arithmetic by scripts/regge/gen_flat_star.py. Limits: second derivatives are those of g at the single point m; the Kuhn triangulation is the standard cubical one; the Gram lengths g(m) are the metric at m, not integrated along edges. Trust checks: the Euclidean metric satisfies the hypotheses, and for sphere-like second derivatives the sum over the 36 incidences is 3, not 0 and not 6 (FlatStarTests.lean).
- **LL-0092.** Part of the 3D convergence of the Regge action (T-RC6), which stays open. For a Riemannian metric g on U and m in U, displace every point k of the star around an edge to k + (ε/2) Γ(k, k) (Γ the Christoffel symbols at m). In each edge class the displaced tetrahedra form a closed fan around the displaced hinge axis that is positively oriented at ε = 0, so the sum of their dihedral angles (computed with the quadratic form g(m)) is 2π for all ε in a neighbourhood of 0 (a neighbourhood, no explicit radius). Uses closed fans of complex numbers, continuity in ε and the lattice result of LL-0078. Limits: one edge star of the standard cubical Kuhn triangulation, one point m; nothing about a triangulation of a manifold or about convergence.
- **LL-0093.** Part of the 3D convergence of the Regge action (T-RC6), which stays open: this is the jet-level statement at one point, not the convergence. For a Riemannian metric g on an open set U of R^3 and any point m of U (no condition on the first derivatives of g), the star of one edge of the standard Kuhn triangulation satisfies JetStarCore: admissible Gram lengths, angle sums 2π in the seven classes, vanishing first-order coefficient, and the sum over the classes of the hinge length (√(g(m)(w, w))) times the second-order coefficient equals minus half the scalar curvature times √det g(m). Proof: the edge polynomial of the jet of g equals that of a flat jet with second derivatives Sdd = ∂∂g - g ΓΓ after displacing the vertices by εΓ(k, k)/2 (edgeC_eq_chr, edgeR_eq_displaced), the displaced flat star has angle sums 2π (LL-0092) so its first- and second-order coefficients vanish (disp_coeffs), the flat identity of LL-0080 applies to Sdd, and the scalar curvature at m is that of the flat jet with Sdd (scalar_eq_flat; the transformation of the curvature under the change of chart is the tensor transformation law cited). Limits: second derivatives at the single point m; standard cubical Kuhn triangulation; no convergence statement, no manifold triangulation; Riemannian (positive definite) signature only. Trust checks: the Euclidean metric and diag(exp x0, 1, 1), whose first derivative at 0 is nonzero so that LL-0080 does not apply to it (ChartChangeTests.lean).
- **LL-0127.** A special case of the convergence theorem of Cheeger, Mueller and Schrader (1984) for one triangulation family (the Kuhn triangulation of a grid); the theorem is cited as described in Christiansen 2011, Section 1, and the comparison with the original paper is pending: it was not read. Part of T-RC6, which stays open for the general statement. For a Riemannian metric g on an open set U of R^3 containing the cube [0,2]^3, the Regge action of the Kuhn triangulation of the grid of mesh 1/N (the sum over the seven edge classes and the hinges with lower corner in [0,1)^3 of the geodesic length of the hinge times its deficit angle 2π minus the sum of the dihedral angles, all computed from the geodesic distance of g) tends to the integral over [0,1]^3 of (R/2)√det g, R the scalar curvature, as N tends to infinity. Proof: the hinge term is -ε^3 √(g(w,w)) c2 + O(ε^4) uniformly on compact sets (hinge_term, from the uniform class-sum expansion and the geodesic length expansion), the seven densities add up to (R/2)√det g at every point (jetStarCore_of_chart, LL-0093), and Riemann sums with sample points in the cells converge for a continuous function. Limits: convergence only, no rate; one chart and the standard cubical Kuhn triangulation, not Cheeger-Müller-Schrader's theorem for arbitrary fine triangulations of a manifold; Riemannian signature only. Trust checks: the hypotheses hold for the flat metric (limit 0) and for the round 3-sphere in stereographic coordinates (ReggeConvergenceTests.lean), and scripts/regge/regge3d_sphere_check.py computes the action from true geodesic lengths for the sphere: S_N = 6.140, 5.353, 4.958, 4.763 at N = 4, 8, 16, 32 against the limit 4.5712, the error halving as N doubles (observation, the theorem gives no rate); the reversed sign and a factor 2 are far from the computed values.
- **LL-0128.** Part of the linearization of 3D Regge calculus (T-RC3), which stays open. For a closed 3-complex K with non-degenerate edge lengths at which every deficit angle δ_e vanishes, and squared lengths varying along ℓ₀² + ε a, the Regge action Σ_e ℓ_e δ_e equals ε²/2 · Σ_e (a_e/(2ℓ₀_e)) δ_e'(0) + O(ε³), where δ_e'(0) is the derivative of the deficit angle along the line. Proof: Regge's equations dS = Σ δ_e dℓ_e (Schläfli's identity) give dS/dε = Σ ℓ_e' δ_e near 0, the dihedral angles are C³ in the squared lengths at admissible tuples, and a one-variable Taylor bound gives the remainder; this is the argument of Christiansen's Proposition 3.2, eq. (75) and its consequence (81), here for an arbitrary closed complex. The statement is non-vacuous: the periodic Kuhn complex of (ℤ/n)³ (n ≥ 3) with its Euclidean lengths is closed, non-degenerate and flat (torus_second_order, Lightlike/Regge/Linear3/TorusComplex.lean), and for the boundary of the 4-simplex with all lengths 1 every deficit angle is 2π − 3 arccos(1/3) > 0 (WrongModel.lean), so the flatness hypothesis is needed. Limits: fixed mesh (the constant M depends on the complex); one line of squared lengths; the identification of the coefficient with ⟨curl^t curl u', u'⟩ (Christiansen's Theorem 3.3) and the limit as the mesh tends to zero are not claimed; the lengths ℓ₀ are required positive on every vertex pair, which only normalises the values off the edges of the complex.
- **LL-0129.** Part of the linearization of 3D Regge calculus (T-RC3), which stays open. For a C^3 symmetric field h of 3x3 matrices on R^3 invariant under integer translations, the integral over the unit cube of -1/4 Sum h_ij eps_ikl eps_jmn d_k d_m h_ln (the Saint-Venant form, the limit of Qn_converges) equals the integral of -1/4 Sum (d_l h_mn)^2 + 1/2 |div h|^2 - 1/2 (div h).(d tr h) + 1/4 |d tr h|^2, one half of the massless Fierz-Pauli Lagrangian of a time-independent field with the term d_m h_nl d_n h_ml written as (div h)^2 (saintVenant_eq_fierzPauli). Proof: the difference of the two densities is the divergence of an explicit periodic C^1 field (fp_identity, a polynomial identity for symmetric h, dh, dd; div_Tfield), and the integral of a periodic divergence over the unit cube is zero (integral_div_periodic, Mathlib's divergence theorem on the box). The hypothesis eq. (2.1) of the reference is the Fierz-Pauli action by name only; the comparison of the density with it is made in the module docstring, not by the source tool. Limits: C^3 periodic symmetric fields on the torus R^3/Z^3, Euclidean indices; that the eta^2 coefficient of the cube integral of (R/2) sqrt(det g) for g = 1 + eta h is half the integral of fpDens (the integral itself being the second eta-derivative) is proved in a later entry (LL-0130), not here; no gauge condition, no mass term. (2.1), is the Fierz-Pauli action); the term-by-term agreement is a statement of the module docstring FierzPauli.lean, not checked by the source tool. Fourth step of the comparison of the linearized Regge action with the Einstein-Hilbert action (T-RC3 in dimension 3, which stays open). For a C-infinity symmetric Z^3-periodic matrix field h on R^3 there are C and eta_0 > 0 such that for |eta| <= eta_0 the integral over the unit cube of (R/2) sqrt(det g) for g = 1 + eta h differs from (eta^2/2) times the integral over the unit cube of the Fierz-Pauli density fpDens(dh) = -1/4 |dh|^2 + 1/2 |div h|^2 - 1/2 div h . d tr h + 1/4 |d tr h|^2 by at most C |eta|^3 (eh_eta_sq_coeff). The first coefficient integrates to zero because it is the divergence of the periodic field S_i = sum_j d_j h_ij - d_i tr h, and the second coefficient differs from fpDens by the divergence of an explicit periodic field T' (F2_eq in CurvaturePoly.lean), so both integrate by Mathlib's divergence theorem on the box with the faces cancelling by periodicity; the pointwise expansion is the uniform second-order expansion of the curvature density (feta_expansion) applied to the jet of h, restricted to the cube. Together with the convergence of the linearized Regge coefficient to the Saint-Venant form and the equality of the Saint-Venant and Fierz-Pauli integrals (LL-0129), this identifies the limit of the linearized Regge coefficient with the second eta-derivative (twice the eta^2 coefficient) of the integrated curvature density of 1 + eta h. Limits: dimension 3; the unit cube with periodic C-infinity symmetric fields (C-infinity as IsCoordMetric requires); the remainder constant is not explicit; the statement is about the integral of the density of the metric 1 + eta h, not about the Regge action, about interpolated or geodesic edge lengths or about a limit of triangulations; two parts of the 3D linearization (RC3) stay open: the envelope step relating geodesic edge lengths to the interpolated ones, and the 3D wrong-model control. Trust checks: the zero field satisfies the hypotheses (eh_eta_sq_coeff_zero); the coefficient for a non-zero field is checked numerically (scripts/regge/regge3d_linearized_check.py: the second eta-derivative of the integrated density equals the Fierz-Pauli integral to six digits for one random field), not in Lean.
- **LL-0131.** A special case, for one periodic family of triangulations, of the convergence theorem of Cheeger, Mueller and Schrader (1984), cited as described in Christiansen 2011, Section 1; the comparison with the original paper is pending: it was not read. For a Z^3-periodic Riemannian metric g on R^3, the Regge action of the periodic Kuhn complex of the 3-torus with mesh 1/N and the geodesic edge lengths of g equals the lattice hinge sum of the convergence theorem on the cube (reggeAction_torus_eq; edges are in bijection with (cell, class) pairs, the dihedral angles are the angles of the squared corner distances, no boundary layer), so it converges to the integral over the unit cube of (R/2) sqrt(det g) (torus_regge_converges). - **LL-0139.** Part of T-RC6, which stays open: this is the 2D check that the deficit angles of the round sphere add up to 4π, not the convergence theorem. For a finite set of triangles in which every edge lies in exactly two triangles, with angles that add up to π in every triangle, the deficit angles 2π minus the sum of the angles around a vertex add up to 2π(V − E + F). The sum of the angles over all vertices is πF (a double count of the vertex–triangle incidences) and 3F = 2E (a double count of the edge–triangle incidences); the angles of a Euclidean triangle add up to π (Mathlib's EuclideanGeometry.angle_add_angle_add_angle_eq_pi). Instance: the octahedron inscribed in the unit sphere (vertices ±e_i, eight equilateral faces, the chordal edge lengths of the sphere) has V = 6, E = 12, F = 8, so the deficit sum is 4π = 2πχ. Wrong model: the octahedron minus one face is not closed and its deficit sum is 2π·6 − π·7 = 5π, not 2π(6 − 12 + 7) = 2π, so the closedness hypothesis is needed. Limits: an abstract set of triangles with Euclidean angles, no Regge action and no convergence statement, no triangulation of a manifold other than this closed one; only the octahedron is checked as an instance.

Notes:

- **LL-0049.** An identity at finite cutoff: the cutoff conditions make the cutoffs on the faces inside the move non-binding. The gauge rule (IsGauge: the vertices, the edges and the gauge triangles form a collapsible 2-complex) is this library's proposal for the 4D analogue of the maximal tree, not a construction from the literature. Non-vacuity: amplitudeGF_move33_example and amplitudeGF_move33_star1 check every hypothesis in the kernel on closed 4-spheres. A perturbed vertex amplitude breaks the identity (ampBad_breaks_move33). Removal of the cutoff and independence of the gauge set are not proven.
- **LL-0050.** An identity at finite cutoff: the cutoff conditions make the cutoffs on the faces inside the move non-binding. The 2-4 move adds one triangle to the gauge set (IsGauge.move24); the 4-2 move is the 2-4 move read backwards (the gauge set is given on the complex after the 4-2 move). Non-vacuity: amplitudeGF_move24_example checks every hypothesis of amplitudeGF_move24 in the kernel on the 1-5 subdivision of the boundary of the 5-simplex, with no gauge triangles, and amplitudeGF_move24_gauge_example does the same for the gauge-fixed form with a gauge set of fourteen triangles (isGauge_T14), so the gauge-fixed statement is instantiated in the kernel; the two sums are shown equal, their value is not computed. There is no wrong-model check for this move; the perturbed amplitude ampBad is checked against the 3-3 move only (LL-0049). Removal of the cutoff and independence of the gauge set are not proven.
- **LL-0051.** An identity at finite cutoff (the cutoff conditions Cut15 make the cutoffs on the faces inside the move non-binding). The 1-5 move adds the four triangles {v, a_0, a_j} to the gauge set (isGauge_move15); the 5-1 move is the 1-5 move read backwards (the gauge set is given on the complex after the 5-1 move). Non-vacuity: amplitudeGF_move15_example checks every hypothesis of amplitudeGF_move15 in the kernel on the boundary of the 5-simplex, with no gauge triangles, and amplitudeGF_move15_gauge_example does the same for the gauge-fixed form with the ten gauge triangles through a vertex (isGauge_starK0), so the gauge-fixed statement is instantiated in the kernel; the two sums are shown equal, their value is not computed. There is no wrong-model check for this move; the perturbed amplitude ampBad is checked against the 3-3 move only (LL-0049). Removal of the cutoff and independence of the gauge set are not proven.
- **LL-0052.** The vertex is the contraction along the edges of K₅ of five Barrett–Crane intertwiners Σ_i ι_i ⊗ ι_i, in the orthonormal intertwiner basis, with no dimension factor per tetrahedron and edge amplitude 1 (a normalisation convention). Baez and Christensen's Riemannian 10j symbol, when nonzero, is negative exactly when the ten spins sum to a half-integer; the vertex here is non-negative for all spins, so the two conventions differ by a sign. bcVertexBC, the vertex times (−1) to the sum of the doubled spins, follows their sign rule; its absolute value is the vertex, and it is ≥ 0 for even and ≤ 0 for odd sums (abs_bcVertexBC, bcVertexBC_nonneg_of_even, bcVertexBC_nonpos_of_odd). The sign rule is taken from Baez and Christensen; that bcVertexBC equals their 10j as they define it is not proven. On the triangle of spin j/2 the 15j symbol is 1/√(j + 1) and the vertex 1/(j + 1), so at spin 1/2 the two conventions give −1/2 and +1/2. Non-vacuity is shown by the value 1 at spin 0 and 1/(j + 1)² on the closed loop of spin j/2. No published table of 10j values was found to compare against.
- **LL-0060.** The twisted cochain complex of a finite 2-complex with an edge connection g and a real representation has d1 ∘ d0 = 0 exactly when g is flat and the face boundaries are closed walks (d1_comp_d0, TwistedCohomology.lean); H² = C²/im d1 is trivial iff d1 is onto (d1_surjective_iff). For SU(2) acting on su(2) = ℝ³ by the adjoint action, varying each edge holonomy along exp(tΦ_e)g_e changes the face holonomies at a flat connection with derivative d1 Φ (holonomy_hasDerivAt), so a first-order change X of the face holonomies is realised exactly when X = d1 Φ (face_variation_iff). The tests: d1 is onto for the disc and not onto for the 2-sphere with one edge, and a non-flat connection breaks d1 ∘ d0 = 0 (TwistedCohomologyTests.lean, real multiplicative coefficients). For SU(2) with the adjoint action, the 2-sphere with one edge and two faces at the trivial connection has d1 not onto and H² ≠ 0 (sphere_su2_H2_nontrivial, TwistedCohomologyTests.lean); on the disc at the trivial connection d1 is onto and every face-holonomy variation is realised (disc_su2_d1_surjective, disc_su2_face_variation), so both sides of the criterion are instantiated for SU(2). Barrett and Naish-Guzman's theorem (§4.4) is existence of the partition function as a distribution; only the finite-dimensional step, d1 = the differential of the holonomy map, is proved here, not the measure-theoretic step. Not covered: the link from H² = 0 to the removal of the Ponzano–Regge cut-off.
- **LL-0061.** The sum rule Σ_{a ≤ 2c} (−1)^a (2a+1) {a c c; c c c} = δ_{c0} follows from the orthogonality of the 6j symbols (racah_sum, from sixJSym_orth_all). For Bing's house with two rooms, BNG §2.4 write the Ponzano–Regge sum as Z = Σ_c Σ_{b ≤ 2c} Σ_{a ≤ 2c} (−1)^(a+b) (2a+1)(2b+1)(2c+1) {a c c; c c c}{b c c; c c c}. Its summand stays of order 1 at large spins, so the sum is not absolutely convergent and its value depends on how it is summed; the model takes its value from a regularisation. Two summations are proved here (Lean uses doubled spins). Room spins first: for each central spin c the sums over a and b run to their full range 2c, where each is δ_{c0}, and any cut-off N on c then gives 1 (bingIterated_eq_one). Simple cut-off Λ on all spins (BNG §2.2): at Λ = 1 the room sums for c = 1 stop at a = 1 instead of 2, which drops the term 5/6 (from {2 1 1; 1 1 1} = 1/6), so Z_1 = 1 + 3 (5/6)² = 37/12 (bingCutoff_two, bingCutoff_two_ne_iterated). 37/12 is one partial sum, not a limit: Z_Λ has no limit (BNG fig. 6, numerical; scripts/spinfoam/bing_house_check.py computes Z_Λ exactly up to Λ = 14, with values between 1 and 8.15 that do not settle). The two values therefore show no inconsistency of the Ponzano–Regge model: the simple cut-off truncates the room sums before 2c, which BNG give as the cause of its divergence, and BNG state (not proved here) that the Turaev–Viro regularisation gives 1 for every q. The sum formula is taken from BNG §2.4; it is not derived in Lean from a state sum on a 2-complex. Not covered: that H² = 0 makes the cut-off removable (BNG §4.4).
- **LL-0066.** For edge spins s (doubled units; edges 01, 02, 03, 12, 13, 23) the integral over SU(2)^4 of Π_e χ_{s e}(g_i g_j⁻¹) equals {s₀₁ s₀₂ s₀₃; s₂₃ s₁₃ s₁₂}² (tetraInt_eq_sixJ_sq). The proof expands each character in the matrix coefficients of the spin representations, integrates them with the Haar measure into products of 3j vectors, and identifies the resulting sum with a 6j symbol up to a sign (ZR_eq). This is Freidel–Louapre's Ponzano–Regge observable of the 1-skeleton of the two-tetrahedron triangulation of S³, eq. (94), read on the dual graph: their group variables sit on the four triangles and the holonomy around an edge is g_i g_j⁻¹ for the two triangles i, j containing it, so the Lean edge ij carries the spin of the edge shared by triangles i and j, and the triads at the Lean vertices are the triangles of the triangulation. Checks: all spins 0 give 1 (tetraInt_zero), all spins 1 (doubled spin 2) give (1/6)² = 1/36 (tetraInt_two), and an inadmissible triad at a vertex gives 0 (tetraInt_eq_zero_of_not_tri, tetraInt_ones_vertex).
- **LL-0067.** The tetrahedron sum over the six doubled edge spins up to a cut-off N has the nonnegative terms Π(s_e+1)·{s₀ s₁ s₂; s₅ s₄ s₃}² (tetraTerm_nonneg). At the doubled spins (0, n, n, n, n, 0) the dimension factor is (n+1)⁴ and the 6j symbol is ±1/(n+1) by the zero-spin formula (sixJSym_zero_left; DLMF eq. 34.5.1 after the 34.5(ii) column symmetry), so the term is (n+1)² (tetraTerm_zeroSpin). Hence the sum is at least (N+1)² (tetraPartition_ge), it is unbounded (tetraPartition_unbounded), and by the monotone-limit criterion it has no limit (not_tetraRemovable). This is the sum without the rescaling M_Λ^{-v} of the simple cut-off of Barrett and Naish-Guzman (§2.2), who do not define M_Λ here; whether the rescaled limit exists is not decided. The tests: the cut-off values 1, 29, 2393/4 at doubled cut-offs 0, 1, 2 are numerical (scripts/spinfoam/tetra_partition_check.py) and lie above (N+1)². Not covered: existence of the sum as a distribution and H² = 0 (Barrett and Naish-Guzman, §4.4), and the link from H² = 0 to the removal of the cut-off.
- **LL-0068.** The three moves 3-3, 2-4 and 1-5 (LL-0049 to LL-0051) are put into one relation GFStep4 on triples (complex, gauge set, cutoffs), with the hypotheses of the three move theorems and a step recut that changes the cutoffs on faces that are not summed (amplitudeGF_congr_cut). A step takes a gauge set to a gauge set (GFStep4.isGauge), and the gauge-fixed amplitude is constant along every chain of steps and their inverses, which are the 4-2 and 5-1 moves (amplitudeGF_eqvGen4). If a gauge set T forces every triangle, the state sum is 1 at every constant cutoff, so it converges as the cutoff is removed (amplitudeGF_tendsto_one_of_forces). Non-vacuity: amplitudeGF_chain_example runs a 1-5 move followed by a 2-4 move on the boundary of the 5-simplex with ten gauge triangles; amplitudeGF_tendsto_starT is the forcing case on the boundary of the 5-simplex. A new result, not from the literature; the gauge fixing generalizes Freidel–Louapre's 3D construction (gr-qc/0212001 §IV): the gauge rule is this library's 4D analogue of their maximal tree (Section IV.B of the paper, the gauge-fixing procedure; the location checked in the registry is the title of Section IV); their independence of the choice of tree is argued there by BRST invariance and is formal. Not proven: finite cutoff only, the cutoffs must be re-chosen by recut between moves and the cutoff conditions are sufficient, not necessary; independence of the gauge set is not proven for gauge sets that do not force every triangle (numerical examples in scripts/spinfoam/gauge_independence_check.py show finite-cutoff dependence for non-forcing sets); the second tree, the global symmetry left at the root vertex, the Faddeev-Popov measure and the limit of the ungauged sum are not treated. Observation, not a proof: for the gauge set of the closed 4-sphere with 24 4-simplices in scripts/spinfoam/gauge_manifold_check.py, which obeys the gauge rule but forces only 38 of its 62 triangles, the cutoff state sum at doubled cutoffs 2, 4, ..., 40 (scripts/spinfoam/gauge_cutoff_limit.py; exact 3j symbols, double-precision contraction, summation-order spread 3e-15 at cutoff 10 and 8e-14 at cutoff 20, not measured at larger cutoffs) changes sign seven times and its largest absolute value grows from 6.0 (cutoffs up to 8) to 33.8 (cutoffs from 12), so numerically the cutoff sums do not settle for that gauge set. The check at 32 and above in higher precision is open. On the boundary of the 5-simplex and on two small 4-spheres every sampled gauge set (3000, 2000 and 2000 random sets) forces every triangle.
- **LL-0069.** Forcing is the rule that a tetrahedron with three of its triangles in the set forces the fourth (Forces); the rule is this library's, used to show that the gauge-fixed state sum is 1 (amplitudeGF_tendsto_one_of_forces). Forces is monotone in the tetrahedra and in the starting set (Forces.mono) and composes (Forces.of_union). The 1-5 move only adds tetrahedra, and each new triangle {v, x, y} is forced by the tetrahedron {v, a_0, x, y} from the four gauge triangles {v, a_0, a_j} (forces_move15). Non-vacuity: forces_move15_example applies it on the boundary of the 5-simplex with the ten triangles through a vertex. Scope: for complexes reached from the boundary of the 5-simplex by 1-5 moves, and in general whenever the hypothesis Forces K K.tris T holds. Open, not proven: the 3-3 and 2-4 moves. A proof that stays inside the six vertices of a 3-3 move cannot work: over the 2^18 sets of the 18 triangles on the six vertices, the closure before the move minus the triangle sigma is not contained in the closure after the move in 3744 cases, and the converse fails in 3744; the map that replaces sigma by tau sends 12016 of the 39942 closed local sets to non-closed ones. What holds locally (exhaustive): all 18 mixed triangles are forced before the move iff they are forced after it. Numerical evidence only (scripts/spinfoam/forcechain.py): random sequences of 3-3, 2-4 and 1-5 moves from the boundary of the 5-simplex kept the gauge set forcing in every sampled case; the inverse 4-2 and 5-1 moves lose forcing of the transported set at some locations, though a forcing gauge set was found directly on every such complex sampled. Counterexample for the 3-3 move (numerical, pinned by counterexample_33() in scripts/spinfoam/forcechain.py): on a closed triangulation of the 4-sphere with 48 simplices there is a collapsible forcing gauge set of size E-V+1 that stops forcing after a 3-3 move with the set unchanged (42 triangles left unforced). Random search found such cases in 11 of about 99,000 trials, so forcing is not preserved by 3-3 for every forcing gauge set. Measured in about 162,000 further trials with random minimal forcing sets: T forces after the 3-3 move exactly when the closure of T under the tetrahedra that do not contain the moved triangle sigma already reaches every other triangle (no forcing step needs sigma); the characterization for the 3-3 move is the separate entry LL-0077 (proved in Lean).
- **LL-0077.** Forcing is this library's rule (a tetrahedron with three of its triangles in the set forces the fourth), used to show that the gauge-fixed state sum is 1. Statement: for a 3-3 move K -> K' that replaces the triangle sigma by tau, and T a set of triangles of K that does not contain sigma and forces every triangle of K, T forces every triangle of K' exactly when the closure of T under the tetrahedra of K that do not contain sigma reaches every triangle of K other than sigma (forces_move33_iff, ForcesIn is forcing by an arbitrary set of tetrahedra). The proof splits the tetrahedra into those common to K and K' and the three that contain sigma (resp. tau). If the common closure is complete, one tetrahedron forces sigma (resp. tau) from the mixed triangles. If it is not, a derivation can leave the common closure only through a tetrahedron sigma + c whose three mixed triangles are in it (a full row), and after the move only through a full row for tau; if both exist, a finite lemma on the eighteen mixed triangles (local33_prop, a Boolean statement over eighteen variables checked by the kernel with decide) shows that adding sigma, or tau, forces nothing more, so at most one of the two complexes forces (forcing_dichotomy). Non-vacuity: forces_move33_example applies it to the boundary of the 5-simplex after a 1-5 and a 2-4 move, with a set of fifteen triangles and the move {0,2,3} -> {4,5,6}, every hypothesis checked by the kernel. Wrong-input control: local33_control shows that without a full row of tau-triangles the conclusion of the finite lemma fails. Scope: the 3-3 move only, with the set T unchanged by the move and not containing sigma; the 2-4 move and the inverse 4-2 and 5-1 moves are not covered. Numerical evidence (scripts/spinfoam/forcechain.py, not part of the proof): a collapsible forcing gauge set of size E-V+1 on a 48-simplex 4-sphere triangulation loses forcing under a 3-3 move (so the second condition is not automatic), and in about 162,000 random trials the characterization held in every case.
- **LL-0081.** Forcing is this library's rule (a tetrahedron with three of its triangles in the set forces the fourth), used to show that the gauge-fixed state sum is 1. Statement: for a 2-4 move K -> K' that removes the tetrahedron sigma (shared by the two 4-simplices sigma + p and sigma + q) and adds the edge {p, q}, a vertex a of sigma, and T a set of triangles of K that forces every triangle of K, the set T together with {a, p, q} (the triangle that the gauge rule adds) forces every triangle of K' exactly when the closure of T under the tetrahedra of K other than sigma already reaches every triangle of K (forces_move24_iff). The move keeps all triangles and adds the four triangles {p, q, s} for s in sigma; the tetrahedra before the move are the common ones and sigma, after it the common ones and the six {p, q, s, s'}. If the common closure is complete, K forces trivially and the new triangles are forced one after the other from {a, p, q} and the triangles {p, s, s'}, {q, s, s'} (forces24_of_common). If not, K can leave the common closure only through sigma, when exactly three of its four triangles are in it, and in that case a finite lemma on the sixteen triangles {p, s, s'}, {q, s, s'} and sigma minus a vertex (local24, a Boolean statement checked by the kernel with decide) shows that the new triangles can be added without forcing anything more in K', so at most one of the two complexes forces (forcing_dichotomy24). Non-vacuity: forces_move24_example applies it to the boundary of the 5-simplex after a 1-5 move, with fourteen triangles, a = 0 and the move {0,1,2,3} -> {5,6}, every hypothesis checked by the kernel. Wrong-input control: local24_control shows that without the hypothesis that exactly three triangles of sigma are in the set, the conclusion of the finite lemma fails. Scope: the 2-4 move only, with the triangle {a, p, q} the only one added to T; the 3-3 move is LL-0077, and the inverse 4-2 and 5-1 moves are not covered (numerical evidence in scripts/spinfoam/forcechain.py shows that the transported set can lose forcing there). Numerical evidence, not part of the proof: in about 526,000 random cases (random complexes, random minimal forcing sets, every 2-4 move and every a) the characterization held in every case.
- **LL-0089.** Forcing is this library's rule (a tetrahedron with three of its triangles in the set forces the fourth). A set T is robust for a complex K (Robust K T) if it forces every triangle of K using the tetrahedra of K with any one of them removed. Statement: if T is robust for K, then T together with the four gauge triangles {v, a_0, a_j} of a 1-5 move is robust for the complex after the move (robust_move15). The old triangles are forced as before, because the 1-5 move only adds tetrahedra; the ten new triangles {v, x, y} are forced by the tetrahedron {v, a_0, x, y}, and when that tetrahedron is the removed one, through a fifth vertex z (the triangles {v, x, z} and {v, y, z} by {v, a_0, x, z} and {v, a_0, y, z}, then {v, x, y} by {v, z, x, y}). Non-vacuity: robust_move15_example applies it on the boundary of the 5-simplex, where the ten triangles through a vertex are robust (Robust K0 starK0, checked by the kernel by robustBy with explicit forcing steps for each of the fifteen removed tetrahedra). Scope: the 1-5 move only. Robustness is not kept in general under the 3-3 and 2-4 moves: robust_not_kept_by_move33 (ForcingRobustCounterexample.lean) proves it for the 3-3 move on an explicit 4-sphere with 20 simplices; for the 2-4 move a random search found a counterexample (a 4-sphere with 30 simplices; 1 of 67,712 random 2-4 locations, MEASURED), checked independently by scripts/spinfoam/robust_counterexample_verify.py but not proved in Lean. Whether the gauge set carried along from the boundary of the 5-simplex stays robust is open: it was robust in every sample (MEASURED; scripts/spinfoam/robust_check.py reproduces short runs, longer runs gave 1,104,480 of 1,104,480 tetrahedra on random complexes, 38,176 of 38,176 3-3 locations and 822 consecutive forward moves) and robust against the removal of any two tetrahedra at 498 of 498 steps, but not against three (267 of 300,000 sampled triples fail, unavoidably, since a triangle outside the set cannot be forced when all its tetrahedra are removed). A robust set keeps forcing under the 2-4 move and under a 3-3 move that does not remove one of its triangles (forces_move24_of_robust, forces_move33_of_robust, with Lemma X forcesIn_common_of_robust_33). Compared with Freidel and Louapre (2003), Section IV.B (read): the paper fixes the translational gauge symmetry of the 3D Ponzano-Regge model with a maximal tree T of the 1-skeleton (V - 1 edges), sets j_e = 0 on the edges of T and collapses them (eqs. (52) and (53)), the result being independent of the tree. Representation: the 4D forcing rule on triangles of a 4D complex, robustness under the 1-5 move, has no counterpart in the paper; it is the library's own combinatorial analogue.
- **LL-0136.** Forcing is this library's rule (a tetrahedron with three of its triangles in the set forces the fourth). (52) and (53)), the result being independent of the tree. Representation: the 4D forcing rule on triangles of a 4D complex, robustness under the 2-4 move, has no counterpart in the paper; it is the library's own combinatorial analogue.
- **LL-0137.** Forcing is this library's rule (a tetrahedron with three of its triangles in the set forces the fourth); a set T is robust for K if it forces every triangle with any one tetrahedron removed. Proof: if the closure A misses a triangle, the complement of A among the common triangles is a nonempty blocking set for the common tetrahedra that avoids T. In the tetrahedron sigma + c_k it meets n_k of the three triangles {s_i, s_j, c_k}. The set A plus sigma is closed under sigma + c_k when n_k is not 1, and A when n_k is not 0; of the three values n_k, at most one is 1 or at most one is 0, so one of the two sets is closed under all tetrahedra but one, and the robustness hypothesis for that tetrahedron puts sigma, or every triangle, in it, a contradiction (lemmaX_abstract, by soundness of forcing). Compared with Freidel and Louapre (2003), Section IV.B (read): the paper fixes the translational gauge symmetry of the 3D Ponzano-Regge model with a maximal tree T of the 1-skeleton (V - 1 edges), sets j_e = 0 on the edges of T and collapses them (eqs. (52) and (53)), the result being independent of the tree. (52) and (53)), the result being independent of the tree. It does not display the identity of this entry. Representation: the identity here is the finite-cutoff recoupling form of the Biedenharn-Elliott step, with explicit cutoff inequalities; that form is the library's own. For each of the 20 cases c, with the inner triangle colour weighted by its dimension jA + 1, lhs_eq_ev_NL expresses the left side as the evaluation (NL c).ev of the reduced network once the cutoffs exceed the triangle inequalities (hypotheses h1, h2, hA, h3); inner_eq is the same for colourings of the vertex set V, and ev_NL_rev says (NL c).ev = (NL c.rev).ev (a gauge transformation and a relabelling). - **LL-0428.** Compared with Freidel and Louapre (2003), Section IV.B (read): the paper fixes the 3D Ponzano-Regge model with a maximal tree of V - 1 edges (eqs. (52), (53)); the 4D gauge rule IsGauge and the count E - V + 1 of its triangles are the library's own analogue, not a statement of the paper. The count is the Euler characteristic of the collapsible complex gaugeCx K T, which is 1 (Collapsible.euler_eq), with the vertices counted with sign +, the edges -, the triangles +, so #T - #edges + #vertices = 1. The value E - V + 1 is the degree of divergence that Bonzom and Smerlak find for a triangulated 4-sphere (comparison pending for this sentence: Bonzom and Smerlak was not read here, the claim about their result is from the earlier inventory). Non-vacuity: gauge sets exist (isGauge_starK0, isGauge_T14, with ten and fourteen triangles; these are checked in the kernel in Tests.lean). The count for a given complex says nothing on whether the gauge-fixed state sum is finite.
- **LL-0497.** For a 4-dimensional complex K and two sets of triangles T, T′ that each force every triangle of K (Forces K K.tris T: iterating the forcing rule, a tetrahedron with three triangles of spin 0 has its fourth triangle and its virtual spin at 0), the gauge-fixed Ooguri state sum amplitudeGF K T cut equals amplitudeGF K T′ cut′ for all cutoffs cut, cut′ (amplitudeGF_eq_of_forces): in a colouring of nonzero weight everything vanishes, so both state sums are 1 (amplitudeGF_eq_one_of_forces). The same holds for two gauge sets (IsGauge, the collapsibility rule) that force (amplitudeGF_eq_of_isGauge_forces). This is a sufficient criterion for independence of the gauge choice, not a theorem about all gauge sets: IsGauge does not imply Forces, and for gauge sets that do not force every triangle the finite-cutoff state sum can depend on the gauge set (numerical evidence, not a Lean statement: scripts/spinfoam/gauge_independence_check.py, five 4-simplices glued non-manifold-wise with four different values at cutoff 1/2, and scripts/spinfoam/gauge_manifold_check.py, a 4-sphere triangulation with 24 4-simplices with state sums 1 and 7/2 at cutoffs 1/2 and 1). The general case of non-forcing gauge sets is an open question and is not claimed. The gauge rule is this library's proposal for the 4D analogue of the maximal tree of Freidel–Louapre (Section III of their paper is the verified location of the 3D gauge fixing), not a construction from the literature, and the independence statement is not in the sources: comparison with a source is not applicable to the criterion and pending for the 3D analogy. Removal of the cutoff is not proven.
- **LL-0505.** Compared with Barrett and Crane (1998), Sections III and IV (read): the paper labels the triangles of a 4-simplex with representations of SU(2) x SU(2) of the form (j, j), called simple (condition (2) of Section III), and builds the vertex of Section IV from them; this is the right-hand side n = m of the statement. The left-hand side, the weak simplicity constraint as the vanishing of Y^H (K - gamma L) Y on the image of the highest-spin embedding at gamma = 0, is the EPRL form of the constraint (the library's Spin4/EPRL.lean), which the paper does not use; the equivalence of the two is this entry's statement, not the paper's. Doubled spins n, m; the constraint is stated for every traceless X in sl(2, C) in the form of the library, eprlMap n m is the embedding of the highest-spin representation and simplicityOp 0 n m X the constraint operator. The statement is the case gamma = 0 of weak_simplicity_iff (the previous simplicity entry): the constraint holds iff n - m = gamma (n + m), which for gamma = 0 is n = m. Hypothesis 0 < n + m. A non-simple representation, spins (1/2, 0), violates it (the test not_simple_half_zero), the simple one, spins (1/2, 1/2), satisfies it (simple_half_half).
- **LL-0587.** Comparison pending: the equality of the state sum with the Ooguri amplitude up to an explicit sign twist is the library's own statement, not a theorem of Engle, Pereira, Rovelli and Livine (2008). Difference from the Ooguri amplitude: the explicit sign eprlGlobalSign, which depends on the order of the vertices (see the entry on the swap phase).
- **LL-0588.** Comparison pending. The proof is the sign (-1)^S of two exchanged rows of a 9j symbol, which cancels over the ten edges of K5. The orientation of K5 inside the 15j symbol (edges from the smaller to the larger position) is a convention of the vertex order, not the orientation of R^4: its dependence is part of the dependence on the vertex order, which is not claimed to vanish.
- **LL-0589.** Comparison pending: a trust check of the library's own statement. The cutoff gives doubled spin at most 1 to the four triangles through the edge {0, 1}; only the zero colouring (weight 1) and the bone colouring (weight 4, weight_col0) survive the triangle constraints, both with the sign +1, so the check does not test the sign twist.
- **LL-0590.** Comparison pending: the library's own statement of the stated dependence on the vertex order (milestone row SF6b: its stated dependence on the vertex order). The checklist item p2 words independence of the vertex order, which this entry does not claim: the dependence is stated. Numerical evidence only (scripts/spinfoam/eprl_order_check.py, docs/notes/sf6b-order-dependence.md): the pure Ooguri amplitude is 5 for the bone cutoff of every edge, the EPRL amplitude is 5 for w - u odd and -3 for w - u even; the Ooguri weights of the bone colourings other than {0, 1} are not proved in Lean.
- **LL-0597.** The four-valent case of Reisenberger's theorem. Reisenberger (1999), §2 Definition 1 and §3 Theorem, read in the arXiv version gr-qc/9809067v1 (HTML rendering). Statement: for four legs of spins j (doubled), a tensor Φ(μ, ν) (μ the self-dual, ν the anti-self-dual projections) whose real and imaginary parts are SU(2)-invariant in μ and in ν (Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2) invariance), and whose components in the tree basis ι_k ⊗ ι_k' vanish for k ≠ k' in the (01)(23) and in the (02)(13) pairings, is c · bcNode j for some c ∈ ℂ (c = 0 allowed). Difference from the source, direction stronger: Definition 1(2) asks the condition for every trivalent tree, which for four legs is three pairings (§3, after eq. (7): X commutes with G_12², G_13² and G_14²); here two pairings suffice. Reisenberger's own proof, eqs. (8)–(16), also uses only G_12² and G_13². Condition 1 of Definition 1 (j_L = j_R on each edge) is built in. Proof: the two diagonal matrices are related by the orthogonal 6j recoupling matrix; its column at the extreme channel l₀ = min(j₀+j₂, j₁+j₃) is a stretched 6j symbol, nonzero for every admissible k by Racah's formula (sixJSym_extreme_ne_zero, from sixJSym_eq_racahW), so all diagonal entries are equal. It does not use the matrix elements β_J of Lévy-Leblond and Lévy-Nahas that Reisenberger's proof needs. Non-vacuity: bcNode itself satisfies every hypothesis (bcNode_hyp), and it is nonzero (coefA_bcNodeR_half). Reisenberger also treats vertices of any valence; only the four-valent case is stated here.

## Dynamical triangulations: Dehn–Sommerville relations

API map: [Lightlike/DynamicalTriangulations/API-map.md](../Lightlike/DynamicalTriangulations/API-map.md)

| ID | Result | Status | Tier | Lean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LL-0055 | The Dehn–Sommerville relations 2N₃ = 5N₄ and 2N₁ − 3N₂ + 6N₃ − 10N₄ = 0 for closed combinatorial 4-manifolds (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.PL.SComplex.IsClosedCombManifold.two_mul_card_eq`, `Lightlike.PL.SComplex.IsClosedCombManifold.dehnSommerville` in [DehnSommerville.lean](../Lightlike/DynamicalTriangulations/DehnSommerville.lean) |
| LL-0059 | The Einstein–Regge action of dynamical triangulations in terms of N₀, N₄ and χ, and its change under the Pachner moves (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.DynamicalTriangulations.dtAction_eq`, `Lightlike.DynamicalTriangulations.dtAction_move`, `Lightlike.DynamicalTriangulations.dtAction_move_one_five` in [Action.lean](../Lightlike/DynamicalTriangulations/Action.lean) |
| LL-0062 | The Einstein–Regge action of 3D dynamical triangulations in terms of N₀ and N₃, and its change under the 3D Pachner moves (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.DynamicalTriangulations.dtAction3_eq`, `Lightlike.DynamicalTriangulations.dtAction3_move23`, `Lightlike.DynamicalTriangulations.dtAction3_move14` in [Action3.lean](../Lightlike/DynamicalTriangulations/Action3.lean) |

Notes:

- **LL-0055.** N_k is the number of faces with k + 1 vertices of a complex in Lightlike.PL. In every dimension n, a face with n vertices of a closed combinatorial n-manifold lies in exactly two top faces and 2N_{n-1} = (n + 1)N_n; in dimension 4 the second relation follows from the Euler characteristic 0 of the vertex links, which are PL 3-spheres. As checks, the boundary of the 5-simplex is a closed combinatorial 4-manifold with N = (6, 15, 20, 15, 6), computed by the kernel, and two 4-simplices glued along a tetrahedron are not a manifold and violate 2N₃ = 5N₄. These are the combinatorial input of four-dimensional dynamical triangulations; the Einstein–Regge action, causal triangulations and ergodicity of the moves are not formalized here. The first relation of the cited eq. (26), the Euler relation N₀ − N₁ + N₂ − N₃ + N₄ = χ, is not included.
- **LL-0059.** For a closed combinatorial 4-manifold the action −κ₂N₂ + κ₄N₄ equals −2κ₂N₀ + (κ₄ − 2κ₂)N₄ + 2κ₂χ, through N₂ = 2N₀ + 2N₄ − 2χ from the Dehn–Sommerville relations (LL-0055). A move with 2 ≤ #σ and 2 ≤ #τ keeps N₀ and χ and changes the action by (#σ − #τ)(κ₄ − 2κ₂), so the 3-3 move leaves it unchanged; the 1-5 move adds one vertex and changes it by −2κ₂ + 4(κ₄ − 2κ₂) (dtAction_move_one_five). Kernel checks: the boundary of the 5-simplex has action −20κ₂ + 6κ₄ (dtAction_sphere), and the formula without the χ term gives −24κ₂ + 6κ₄ there, the wrong value. Not covered: the Lorentzian action of causal dynamical triangulations, which weighs (4,1) and (3,2) simplices differently. As a non-vacuity check, the 1-5 move of the boundary of the 5-simplex with a new vertex changes the action by −2κ₂ + 4(κ₄ − 2κ₂) (sphere7_dtAction_move), and a 2-4 move on the result by 2(κ₄ − 2κ₂), the formula with #σ = 4 and #τ = 2 (sphere7_dtAction_move24).
- **LL-0062.** For a closed combinatorial 3-manifold the Dehn–Sommerville relations give N₂ = 2N₃ and N₁ = N₀ + N₃, so χ = 0 (dehnSommerville3, card_tris, card_edges, euler_eq_zero in DehnSommerville3.lean), and the action −κ₁N₁ + κ₃N₃ equals −κ₁N₀ + (κ₃ − κ₁)N₃. The 2-3 move changes it by κ₃ − κ₁ and the 1-4 move by 3κ₃ − 4κ₁. Checks: after a 1-4 move on the boundary of the 4-simplex a 2-3 move applies and changes the action by κ₃ − κ₁ (dtAction3_S3_14_23); the boundary of the 4-simplex has counts (5, 10, 10, 5) and action −10κ₁ + 5κ₃; two tetrahedra glued along a triangle violate N₂ = 2N₃ and are not a combinatorial manifold (Tests3.lean).

| LL-0124 | A bubble of one color is a line with two ends, and a bubble of p colors is a connected colored graph in dimension p - 1 (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.bubble_singleton`, `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.card_bubble_singleton`, `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.restrict_isConnected` in [Bubble.lean](../Lightlike/GFT/Bubble.lean) |
| LL-0148 | The dual of a connected colored graph is a normal pseudo-manifold (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.dual_isNormalPseudoManifold`, `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.dual_isSimplicial` in [Dual.lean](../Lightlike/GFT/Dual.lean) |
| LL-0149 | The link of a simplex of the dual of a colored graph is the dual of a bubble, as a colored graph (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.linkIso`, `Lightlike.GFT.ColoredGraph.link_isDual_of_two_le` in [DualLink.lean](../Lightlike/GFT/DualLink.lean) |

Notes:

- **LL-0123.** The definitions and checked examples behind LL-0148 and LL-0149, which state Gurau's Theorems 2 and 1 over them: under the catalogue rule (an entry only for a result that a paper or book would state as a theorem) it would get no entry today; it keeps its number. Definitions after Gurau 2010, Section 5: a colored graph of dimension D has vertices of two orientations and lines of D + 1 colors, exactly one line of each color at every vertex, every line joining opposite orientations (ColoredGraph: one fixed-point-free involution per color and an orientation that each involution flips); a p-bubble is a connected component of the subgraph of the lines with colors in a set of size p (bubble: the vertices reachable in #V steps); the dual complex has one k-simplex for each (D - k)-bubble (Theorem 2, eq. (38)). Proved: the computed bubble is the connected component, i.e. the set reachable along lines with colors in S (mem_bubble_iff); the 0-bubbles are the vertices (nBubbles_empty); a colored graph has an even number of vertices, so none exists on three (even_card, not_nonempty_coloredGraph_fin3). For D = 2 the dual has #V triangles, 3#V/2 edges and one vertex for each bicolored cycle, so 2χ = 2(B01 + B02 + B12) - #V (twoChi2): the graph with two vertices and three lines gives χ = 2, the sphere (twoChi2_theta), and a graph with six vertices gives χ = 0, the torus (twoChi2_torus), both by decide +kernel. Wrong model: a vertex with two lines of one color makes the graph not properly colored (IsProper, badLines_not_proper). Not proved here: Gurau's Theorem 1 (the p-bubbles are the links of the (n-p)-simplices of the dual) and Theorem 2 (the dual is a normal simplicial pseudo-manifold), which are LL-0149 and LL-0148, with their differences named there; that twoChi2 is the Euler characteristic of a closed surface built from the dual (only the face count is formalized); that the Euler characteristic of a connected graph is even. The D = 2 genus statement is standard (ribbon graphs and crystallization theory) and is not in Gurau 2010. Only two examples are computed, not a general theorem.
- **LL-0124.** A supporting lemma of LL-0148 and LL-0149 (Gurau 2010, Theorems 2 and 1): under the catalogue rule (an entry only for a result that a paper or book would state as a theorem) it would get no entry today; it keeps its number. For a colored graph, the bubble of the single color c at v is {v, inv c v} (the 1-bubbles are the lines), so it has exactly two vertices because inv c has no fixed point: the non-branching condition for the dual. A vertex lies in its own bubble (purity), in a connected graph any two vertices are joined by a chain of lines (strong connectivity), and the lines of p colors restricted to a bubble form a colored graph of dimension p - 1 (ColoredGraph.restrict) that is connected (restrict_isConnected): the graph-side shadow of the condition that the links of the dual are pseudo manifolds. These formalize the definitions of Gurau 2010, Sections 2 and 5, for the graph only. Limits: Theorem 1 (the p-bubbles are the link graphs of the (n - p)-simplices) and Theorem 2 (the dual is a normal simplicial pseudo manifold) are not stated here; they are LL-0149 and LL-0148, on a dual built as a graded poset, because a set of faces cannot represent the multiset gluing of eqs. (37) and (38) (in the graph with two vertices and three lines both top simplices have the same vertex set). Trust check: in that graph the 1-bubble of color 0 at 0 is {0, 1} and differs from the 0-bubble.
- **LL-0148.** Gurau (2010), Theorem 2: any connected colored graph is dual to a normal simplicial pseudo-manifold. The dual Delta_G is built as a graded poset of pairs (S, B) of a set of colors and a bubble of the other colors, ordered by inclusion of the colors and reverse inclusion of the bubble, with the number of colors as rank, so that two simplices with the same vertex set stay distinct (as the source's multiset requires). For a connected graph of dimension D it is pure, non-branching (a simplex of rank D, the dual of a line, is a face of exactly two top simplices), strongly connected, and normal (the link of every simplex of rank at most D - 1 is a pseudo-manifold), and the lower interval of every simplex is the powerset of its colors (dual_isSimplicial), which is the simplicial structure. Limits: the vertex sets of the simplices are not part of the structure, so a simplicial complex in the sense of a set of vertex sets is not claimed (it fails already for the graph with two vertices and three lines); Theorem 1 (the link of a simplex is the dual of the bubble, as a colored graph) is not part of this entry. Comparison with the source: the statement of Theorem 2 and the definitions of its Section 2 were read in arXiv:1006.0714 (the proof was not compared). Differences from the source: (1) Gurau states a normal simplicial pseudo-manifold, a collection of subsets of a vertex set that may repeat (his eq. (21) is the graph with two vertices and four lines), while this entry states it for a graded poset with indexed simplices, with the simplicial property only as Boolean lower intervals; the two are not proved equivalent. (2) Gurau defines a pseudo-manifold as normal if all its links are pseudo manifolds; here normality is asked only for the links of simplices of rank at most D - 1 (links of dimension at least 1), so the links of the simplices of rank D (two points) and D + 1 (empty) are not required to be pseudo-manifolds, a range the source does not restrict. The maintainers approved both differences on 17 November 2026 as differences of representation (asking normality for the links of rank at most D - 1 is the standard definition); the agreement of the indexed form with the set-of-faces form when no simplices repeat is proved in Lightlike/GFT/DualVertexSets.lean (le_iff_vertexSet_subset_of_injective, vertexSetOrderIso).
- **LL-0149.** Gurau (2010), Theorem 1: the p-bubbles of a colored graph are the link graphs of the (n - p)-simplices of the gluing. For a simplex sigma = (S, B) of the dual Delta_G (a set S of colors and a bubble B of the other colors) the simplices that contain sigma are in order-preserving bijection with the simplices of the dual of the colored graph G' of the lines of the colors outside S restricted to B (ColoredGraph.restrict), by linkIso, and the bijection lowers the rank by the rank of sigma (linkIso_rk); link_isDual (a supporting lemma, for every simplex that does not have all colors, p >= 1) gives it with the colors outside S enumerated in increasing order, and link_isDual_of_two_le states it in the range of the source, at least two colors outside S (p >= 2). The bijection is built from the two maps linkTo and linkOf, inverse to each other, and the bubbles of the restricted graph are the bubbles of G (mem_bubble_restrict). Limits: the link is the set of simplices containing sigma with the induced order, as a graded poset; the vertex sets of the simplices are not part of the structure; the statement is for the colored graph restricted to a bubble, not for the stranded graph of Gurau's Section 3.1. Comparison with the source: the statement of Theorem 1 was read in arXiv:1006.0714, Section 5 (the proof was not compared). Differences from the source: Gurau states that for p >= 2 the p-bubbles are the link graphs (stranded graphs of his Section 3.1) of the (n - p)-simplices, an identification of graphs; this entry gives an order isomorphism between the link poset and the dual of the colored graph of the bubble, with no stranded graph, in the range p >= 2 that the source states. The maintainers approved this form on 17 November 2026, as a difference of representation. If stranded graphs are defined in the library, their equivalence with this form becomes a task.

## Stationary phase for integrals with a complex phase

API map: [Lightlike/Oscillatory/API-map.md](../Lightlike/Oscillatory/API-map.md)

| ID | Result | Status | Tier | Lean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LL-0126 | Stationary phase with complex phase, leading term (Hörmander, Theorem 7.7.5) (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Oscillatory.stationary_phase`, `Lightlike.Oscillatory.stationary_phase_of_isOpen` in [StationaryPhase.lean](../Lightlike/Oscillatory/StationaryPhase.lean) |
| LL-0468 | Stationary phase with complex phase, leading term, for phase and amplitude on Fin n -> R (Hörmander, Theorem 7.7.5): the integral of a e^{i tau phi} is the sum over the nondegenerate critical points of e^{i tau phi(x0)} (2 pi/tau)^{n/2} det(-iH)^{-1/2} a(x0) up to O(tau^{-n/2-1}) (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Oscillatory.stationary_phase_pi` in [StationaryPhase.lean](../Lightlike/Oscillatory/StationaryPhase.lean) |
| LL-0469 | The Maslov phase of a real diagonal Hessian - the inverse square root of det(-i diag(d)), with the branch fixed by the principal roots of the eigenvalues, is the product of |d_i|^{-1/2} e^{i pi sgn(d_i)/4} (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Oscillatory.invSqrtDet_neg_I_real_diagonal` in [QuadraticPhaseTests.lean](../Lightlike/Oscillatory/QuadraticPhaseTests.lean) |

Notes:

- **LL-0126.** Theorem 7.7.5 of Hormander (ALPDO I), leading term: for a smooth phase phi on EuclideanSpace R^n and a smooth compactly supported amplitude a, with Im phi >= 0 on the support, the critical points in the support (Im phi = 0, d phi = 0) forming a finite set K of nondegenerate points (det(-iH) != 0), the integral of a e^{i lambda phi} equals the sum over K of e^{i lambda phi(x0)} (2 pi / lambda)^{n/2} det(-iH(x0))^{-1/2} a(x0) up to O(lambda^{-n/2-1}); the square root is the product of the principal roots of the eigenvalues of -iH (invSqrtDet). Away from the critical points the integral is O(lambda^{-k}) for every k (Theorem 7.7.1, nonstationary_phase). stationary_phase assumes Im phi >= 0 on the support of a only, so critical points on the boundary of the support are allowed; stationary_phase_of_isOpen assumes it on an open set containing the support, as Hormander does. The higher-order terms of the expansion in Theorem 7.7.5 are not stated.
- **LL-0468.** The same statement as LL-0126 (stationary_phase, on EuclideanSpace R^n) for functions on the product type Fin n -> R, with Mathlib's Lebesgue measure on the product. Hypotheses: phi smooth with Im phi >= 0 on the support of the smooth compactly supported amplitude a; the critical points in the support (Im phi = 0 and d phi = 0) form a finite set K and are nondegenerate (det(-i H) not zero); critical points on the boundary of the support are allowed, where a is flat. The square root is invSqrtDet, the product of the principal roots of the eigenvalues of -iH, not the principal root of the determinant. Comparison with Hörmander, ALPDO I, Theorem 7.7.5 pending: the book was not read at the theorem; the registry verifies only the chapter. The Fresnel integral check is fresnel_bump (QuadraticPhaseTests.lean); the wrong-model check, that a degenerate phase i x^4 changes the order so the non-degeneracy hypothesis cannot be dropped, is stationary_phase_needs_nondegenerate (StationaryPhaseTests.lean).
- **LL-0469.** For real nonzero d_i, invSqrtDet (-I • diagonal d) = prod_i |d_i|^{-1/2} exp(i pi/4 * (1 if d_i > 0 else -1)), that is |det A|^{-1/2} e^{i pi sgn A / 4} for A = diag d. The comparison with Hörmander, ALPDO I, (3.4.6) and section 7.7 is pending (the book was not read there; the registry verifies only the chapter). Only the real diagonal case is proved; the general real symmetric case follows by diagonalisation but is not stated here. invSqrtDet is the library's definition (eigenvalue branches), not a principal root of the determinant.

Notes:

- **LL-0133.** The FLRW metric -dt² + a(t)² dx² / (1 + k|x|²/4)² in isotropic coordinates, for every real k, on the set where t ∈ I and 1 + k|x|²/4 > 0 (the Poincaré ball for k < 0, all of ℝ³ for k ≥ 0), with a smooth positive a on an open interval I and the perfect fluid (ρ + p) u u + p g at rest in the chart: G + Λ g = 8πG T holds there iff Friedmann's first and second equations hold at every t ∈ I (units c = 1). The same statement with Physlib's FirstOrderFriedmann and SecondOrderFriedmann at c = 1 on the right is flrw_einstein_iff_physlib_friedmann in Lightlike/Cosmology/FLRWPhyslib.lean. The continuity equation follows (friedmann_continuity, for G ≠ 0). Trust checks: de Sitter with k = 0 solves the equations iff H² = 8πGρ/3; Einstein's static dust universe with k = 1 iff Λ = 1/a² = 4πGρ; with k = -1 there is no static dust solution; scripts/flrw_check.py recomputes the Ricci and Einstein components with sympy and shows that the metric with the sign of k flipped fails them. Limits: a statement in one chart, not on a manifold I × Σ; for k > 0 the chart misses one point of the 3-sphere; ρ and p depend on t only and the fluid is comoving, by assumption. The comparison with the cited source is pending.
- **LL-0191.** Kar and SenGupta's (12), d theta/d lambda + theta^2/3 + sigma^2 - omega^2 = -R_ab v^a v^b for a timelike geodesic congruence, and (16), convergence if R_ab v^a v^b + sigma^2 - omega^2 >= 0. In coordinates on the FLRW chart: the comoving field u = d_t has nabla_j u^i = H delta^i_j on spatial indices and 0 otherwise (no shear, no rotation), is geodesic, and has expansion theta = 3 a'/a; along it d theta/dt + theta^2/3 = -R_00. Minkowski (a = 1, k = 0): theta = 0. de Sitter (a = e^{Ht}, k = 0): theta = 3H constant while R_00 = -3H^2 < 0, so the convergence condition fails and the congruence does not focus (the GE3 checks). Focusing: if theta' <= -theta^2/m on [0, L) and theta(0) < 0 then L <= m/|theta(0)| (the lemma Lightlike.focusing, Spacetime/RiccatiFocusing.lean). Limits: coordinates and constant fields; the Raychaudhuri equation for a general geodesic congruence on a manifold and the exponential map are not here.
- **LL-0222.** For a positive scale factor a on an open interval (t1, t2) with Friedmann's second equation with zero cosmological constant, the strong energy condition (rho + 3p at least zero) and a'(t0) > 0 at a time t0 in the interval: t0 - t1 is at most a(t0)/a'(t0); and for Friedmann's first equation with k at least zero and zero cosmological constant, if a tends to zero as t decreases to t1 then rho tends to infinity. With Carroll's hypotheses rho > 0 and p >= 0 the age is strictly less than a(t0)/a'(t0) (bigBang_age_lt_of_pos_density), and for every k, if rho(t0) > 0 and a tends to zero then rho tends to infinity, since rho(t) a(t)^2 >= rho(t0) a(t0)^2 for t <= t0 (bigBang_density_tendsto_atTop_of_pos); the Milne universe a = t, k = -1, rho = 0 shows that the positivity of the density is needed (milne_friedmann). Limits: real-variable statements; that the interval is maximal (so that a tends to zero at its left end) is not proved. Compared with Carroll's lecture notes, p. 224 (after eq. (8.41); 'by (8.35) we must have a'' < 0') and p. 225; see docs/notes/co1-carroll-comparison.md.
- **LL-0226.** For a C^2 scale factor a > 0 on (t1, t2) solving both Friedmann equations with Lambda = 0, rho + 3p >= 0 and p <= rho, expanding at t0: either a -> 0 as t decreases to t1, or a', a'', rho and p are bounded on (t1, t0] (bigBang_singularity), so a singularity at the left end of the interval is at a = 0. Proof: ((a'^2 + k) a^4)' = 2 a' a^3 (a a'' + 2(a'^2 + k)) = 8 pi G a' a^5 (rho - p) >= 0 (Carroll's (8.34), a''/a + 2(a'/a)^2 + 2k/a^2 = 4 pi G (rho - p), which combines (8.35) and (8.36)), so rho a^6 stays bounded in the past while a >= L > 0. The hypothesis p <= rho is needed: a = 1 + sqrt t on (0, infinity), k = 0, solves both equations with rho > 0, p > 0, a' > 0, a'' < 0, and a' -> infinity as t -> 0 while a -> 1 (onePlusSqrt_friedmann); hence p > rho somewhere (onePlusSqrt_not_dominant). Carroll's 'we necessarily reach a singularity at a = 0' (p. 224) under rho > 0, p >= 0 alone fails for this a.
- **LL-0227.** Carroll's setting (8.21)-(8.23), p = w rho with constant w (w >= 0 at p. 224), for every w > -1/3: for a C^2 scale factor a > 0 on (t1, t2) solving both Friedmann equations with Lambda = 0, rho >= 0, p = w rho, expanding at t0, either a -> 0 as t decreases to t1 or a', a'', rho, p are bounded on (t1, t0]. Proof: (a'^2 + k) a^{1+3w} is constant (its derivative a' a^{3w} (2 a a'' + (1 + 3w)(a'^2 + k)) vanishes by (8.35), (8.36)), i.e. rho a^{3(1+w)} is constant as in (8.23). Reading (a) of p. 224, any rho > 0, p >= 0, is false (onePlusSqrt_friedmann, LL-0226); reading (b), this setting, is proved here.
- **LL-0330.** CO1 (G1-023), the three trust checks of the milestone at the level of Einstein's equations (IsEinsteinSolution), through flrw_einstein_iff_friedmann (LL-0133). deSitter_example shows the hypotheses are met (H = 1, ρ = 1, G = 3/8π). The static-universe checks have the Friedmann-level forms einsteinStatic_friedmann_iff and not_einsteinStatic_friedmann_of_negCurvature in the same file. The cosmological constant of de Sitter is carried by the fluid (Λ = 0, ρ = -p = ρΛ). The comparison with Carroll is pending: only eq. (8.36) is a recorded verified location.
- **LL-0331.** CO1 (G1-023), the link to Physlib's Friedmann definitions that the milestone asks for. The two forms of each equation agree at c = 1 for functions of the real time coordinate read as functions on Physlib's Time (onTime); this file only restates flrw_einstein_iff_friedmann (LL-0133) with Physlib's equations on the right. Spatial curvature k is any real number, as in LL-0133.
