| LL-0143 | Closed combinatorial surfaces are PL homeomorphic exactly when they have the same orientability and Euler characteristic (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Surfaces.plHomeomorphic_iff`, `Lightlike.Surfaces.existsUnique_plHomeomorphic_stdModel` in [PLClassify.lean](../Lightlike/Surfaces/PLClassify.lean) |
| LL-0144 | Closed combinatorial surfaces are related by 2D bistellar moves to exactly one standard model, determined by orientability and Euler characteristic (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Surfaces.classify`, `Lightlike.Surfaces.isSurface_iff_classify`, `Lightlike.Surfaces.classify_unique`, `Lightlike.Surfaces.exists_eqvGen_stdModel_iff` in [Classify.lean](../Lightlike/Surfaces/Classify.lean) |
| LL-0461 | The standard models of closed surfaces are fixed by orientability and Euler characteristic: the sphere with g handles has χ = 2 − 2g, the connected sum of k + 1 projective planes has χ = 1 − k, and two standard models of the same orientability and the same Euler characteristic are equal (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Surfaces.stdModel_eq_of_inv`, `Lightlike.Surfaces.euler2_stdModel_true`, `Lightlike.Surfaces.euler2_stdModel_false` in [Classify.lean](../Lightlike/Surfaces/Classify.lean) |

Notes:

- **LL-0141.** A closed combinatorial surface (IsSurface: every edge in two triangles, every vertex link connected, the 1-skeleton connected) generates a closed combinatorial 2-manifold in the sense of the PL area: the link of every vertex is a connected graph with two edges at every vertex (isCycleGraph_lk2), hence a PL 1-sphere by the previous entry (IsSurface.isClosedCombManifold). The edge counts come from the closedness condition by the bijection between the triangles through an edge and the edges of the vertex link. Limits: this is the direction from the surface conditions to the PL conditions; the converse, that a closed combinatorial 2-manifold has these properties, is not proved here. Check: the 6-vertex projective plane and the 9-vertex torus of the surface checks satisfy the hypothesis.
- **LL-0142.** A bistellar move κ(σ, τ) on the complex generated by the triangles L of a closed combinatorial 2-manifold has #σ + #τ = 4 and is one of the three kinds: a triangle is subdivided by a new vertex (sub13), an edge is flipped (flip22), or a vertex of degree three is removed (the inverse of sub13); in each case the generating triangles of the result are L with the corresponding move of the Ponzano–Regge API applied (exists_move2, eqvGen_bnew_sub, eqvGen_bnew_flip, eqvGen_bnew_unsub). By Pachner's theorem in the stellar form (LL-0023), closed surfaces whose complexes are stellar equivalent are therefore related by a chain of such moves on their triangles placed in V ⊕ ℕ, where the extra vertices are the new vertices of the moves (eqvGen_move2_of_stellarEquiv). This is the two-dimensional case of pachner3 for the 3D moves. The converse direction is stellarEquiv_of_eqvGen_move2. Limits: it applies to closed surfaces (IsSurface), through the identification of the previous entry; the triangles are placed in V ⊕ ℕ, and relabelling keeps the Euler characteristic and orientability (euler2_mapTri, isOrientable_mapTri_iff). Check: the theorem applies to the two certificate tori (TestsPL).
- **LL-0143.** Two closed combinatorial surfaces L and L' on an infinite vertex type have PL homeomorphic generated complexes exactly when they are both orientable or both not and have the same Euler characteristic (plHomeomorphic_iff), and every closed surface is PL homeomorphic to exactly one standard model, a sphere with handles or a connected sum of projective planes (existsUnique_plHomeomorphic_stdModel). The PL statement comes from composing the PL form of Pachner's theorem (LL-0065, Lickorish Theorem 5.9) with the classification of closed surfaces up to 2D bistellar moves (the surface API, which classifies by orientability and Euler characteristic, in the sense of the chapter of Moise cited; the Surfaces proof is by moves and is not Moise's): a PL homeomorphism gives a bistellar equivalence (LL-0065), which is a chain of 2D moves on the triangles by the previous entry and so preserves orientability and Euler characteristic; conversely a chain of 2D moves from each surface to its standard model gives stellar equivalence (stellarEquiv_of_eqvGen_move2) and so a PL homeomorphism, with the two placements of the model related by relabelling. The vertex type is infinite as a hypothesis because the moves of a chain need new vertices. Limits: the statement is about the PL homeomorphism of the combinatorial realisations of closed surfaces; it does not say that a PL homeomorphism of such surfaces maps given triangulations in a particular way, and it is not the classification of topological surfaces. Differences from the cited sources: the PL homeomorphism is defined by a PL bijection of the realisations, not by a simplicial isomorphism of subdivisions as in Lickorish, and the equivalence of the two definitions is not formalised; Lickorish Theorem 5.9 has not been compared with the statement word for word, and the theorem number of the Moise chapter has not been verified (only the chapter is located). The comparison with the cited source is pending. Check: the 9-vertex torus and Möbius' 7-vertex torus, with no move between them given, are PL homeomorphic (T9_plHomeomorphic_T7); the torus is not PL homeomorphic to the projective plane, to the sphere or to the Klein bottle (TestsPL).
- **LL-0144.** Every closed combinatorial surface (IsSurface) on an infinite vertex type is related by finitely many 2D bistellar moves and their inverses (Move2) to a placed standard model, a sphere with handles stdModel true g or a connected sum of k + 1 projective planes stdModel false k (classify, isSurface_iff_classify); the model is unique, because the moves preserve orientability and the Euler characteristic, which determine it (classify_unique, exists_eqvGen_stdModel_iff). This is the combinatorial form of the classification of compact connected 2-manifolds, which Moise states up to homeomorphism (Moise, chapter The classification of compact connected 2-manifolds, as cited for LL-0024); the statement and the proof here are about moves, by connected sums with the 6-vertex projective plane and the 9-vertex torus and Dyck's relation, and are not Moise's. The classification up to PL homeomorphism is the entry LL-0143. Limits: closed surfaces are finite sets of triangles with every edge in two triangles, every vertex link connected and the 1-skeleton connected; no boundary. Check: the 6-vertex projective plane, the 9-vertex torus and Möbius' 7-vertex torus are related to their standard models, and the Klein bottle, the sphere, a single triangle and two disjoint spheres are rejected as models of the torus (Surfaces/Tests.lean).
- **LL-0461.** Comparison pending: no source was read at a cited location for this entry. The statements are the classical Euler characteristics of the orientable surface of genus g (2 - 2g) and of the connected sum of k + 1 projective planes (1 - k), here for the library's combinatorial models stdModel true g and stdModel false k (a sphere with g handles from the 9-vertex torus piece T9, and k + 1 copies of the 6-vertex projective plane P6), with euler2 the Euler characteristic of the combinatorial complex. stdModel_eq_of_inv says that b = b' and n = n' follow from equal orientability and equal Euler characteristic; it is the injectivity half of LL-0144 (classify_unique). The two Euler-characteristic theorems are in Models.lean, stdModel_eq_of_inv in Classify.lean (the entry file is the one of the main statement). No hypotheses beyond those stated in the Lean theorems; no unproved hypothesis.

| LL-0152 | The Lie-derivative form of the smeared momentum constraint equals the ADM form with the covariant divergence of the momentum (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Canonical.momentumConstraint_eq_adm_of_smooth` in [MomentumADM.lean](../Lightlike/Canonical/MomentumADM.lean) |
| LL-0153 | The bracket of two smeared Hamiltonian constraints is the smeared momentum constraint of the shift given by the inverse metric applied to the antisymmetrized derivatives of the lapses (see note) | proven | established | `Lightlike.Canonical.bracket_hamiltonian_hamiltonian_of_smooth` in [HamiltonianHHBracket.lean](../Lightlike/Canonical/HamiltonianHHBracket.lean) |

Notes:

- **LL-0146.** {D[xi], D[eta]} = D[[xi, eta]] for smooth compactly supported shifts, smooth h and continuous pi, with D[xi] = integral of pi^ij (L_xi h)_ij and the bracket computed with Gateaux derivatives along compactly supported variations (the pi-gradient of D[xi] is L_xi h). Differences, approved by the maintainers (17 November 2026): (a) same setting as the source, (b) partial, (c) convention, (d) and (e) representation (compared with Thiemann, arXiv:gr-qc/0110034, §I.1.1, eqs. (I.1.1.27), (I.1.1.28), (I.1.1.36), (I.1.1.37) (the lecture-note version of the cited book); Hojman-Kuchar-Teitelboim 1976 has not been read): (a) C^infinity data and compactly supported test fields; (b) one global chart R^d, no manifold and no foliation; (c) units 16 pi G = 1 and the kinetic coefficient 1/(d-1) of the Hamiltonian density (1/2 for d = 3), which does not enter this bracket; (d) the momentum constraint in the Lie-derivative form, equal to the ADM form -2 xi_i pi^ij_|j by an integration by parts, formalised as `Lightlike.Canonical.momentumConstraint_eq_adm_of_smooth`; (e) the bracket is defined through pi-gradients and Gateaux derivatives, and the signs of the bracket and of the Lie bracket are fixed by admBracket and lieBracket. The result is partial until the hypersurface version (task F11) replaces the one global chart (b).
- **LL-0147.** {D[xi], H[N]} = H[xi^k d_k N] for smooth compactly supported xi and N, smooth data with positive definite h, with the Hamiltonian density (tr (h pi h pi) - (tr h pi)^2/(d-1))/sqrt(det h) - sqrt(det h) R computed from the coordinate scalar curvature of the geometry API. The proof shows that the scalar curvature is a smooth function of the 2-jet of the metric, that it is covariant under the flow of xi (the library's finite pullback law), that the kinetic term is a scalar density, and differentiates the smeared constraint under the integral sign. Differences, approved by the maintainers (17 November 2026): (a) same setting as the source, (b) partial, (c) convention, (d) and (e) representation (compared with Thiemann, arXiv:gr-qc/0110034, §I.1.1, eqs. (I.1.1.27), (I.1.1.28), (I.1.1.36), (I.1.1.37) (the lecture-note version of the cited book); Hojman-Kuchar-Teitelboim 1976 has not been read): (a) C^infinity data, positive definite h and compactly supported test fields; (b) one global chart R^d, no manifold and no foliation; (c) units 16 pi G = 1 and the kinetic coefficient 1/(d-1) in dimension d (1/2 for d = 3), the one for which the algebra of the constraints closes; (d) the momentum constraint in the Lie-derivative form; (e) the bracket is defined through pi-gradients and Gateaux derivatives, and the signs of the bracket and of the Lie bracket are fixed by admBracket and lieBracket. A grid computation in dimension two (scripts/adm_algebra_check.py) agrees to three digits. The result is partial until the hypersurface version (task F11) replaces the one global chart (b).
- **LL-0152.** For smooth data with positive definite h and symmetric pi and a smooth compactly supported shift xi, the integral of pi^ij (L_xi h)_ij equals the integral of -2 xi_i pi^ij_|j with xi_i = h_ik xi^k and the covariant divergence of Lightlike.christoffel; pointwise the difference is 2 d_j (pi^ij xi_i), and the integral of a derivative of a compactly supported function is zero. The representation difference (d) of the CA1 brackets: approved by the maintainers as representation (17 November 2026). Same setting as the source; one global chart (b) as in the other CA1 results.
- **LL-0153.** {H[N], H[M]} = D[Y] with Y^i = h^ij (N d_j M - M d_j N) for smooth compactly supported N and M, smooth data with positive definite h and symmetric pi, in dimension d at least 2, with the Hamiltonian density (tr (h pi h pi) - (tr h pi)^2/(d-1))/sqrt(det h) - sqrt(det h) R, D[xi] the integral of pi^ij (L_xi h)_ij, and the bracket computed with Gateaux derivatives along compactly supported variations. The proof differentiates the first-order form of H[N] along M times the pi-gradient of H[M], antisymmetrizes, and reduces the remaining coefficient to -2 times the covariant divergence of pi by an index computation with the Christoffel symbols; the ADM form of the momentum constraint closes the argument. Compared with Thiemann, arXiv:gr-qc/0110034, sec. I.1.1, eq. (I.1.1.37) (the lecture-note version of the cited book), same signs and structure function; Hojman-Kuchar-Teitelboim 1976 has not been read. Differences, approved by the maintainers (17 November 2026): (a) same setting as the source; (b) partial: one global chart R^d, no manifold and no foliation (task F11); (c) convention: units 16 pi G = 1 and the kinetic coefficient 1/(d-1); (d) representation: D[xi] in the Lie-derivative form, equal to the ADM form by Lightlike.Canonical.momentumConstraint_eq_adm_of_smooth; (e) representation: the bracket through pi-gradients and Gateaux derivatives. The result is partial until the hypersurface version (task F11) replaces the one global chart (b).

Notes:

- **LL-0163.** For a strongly continuous one-parameter group of unitaries U(t) on a complex Hilbert space, the generator A psi = -i d/dt U(t) psi at t = 0, on the vectors where the derivative exists, is self-adjoint: A is contained in its adjoint and its adjoint in A. This is one direction of Stone's theorem; the converse, that every self-adjoint operator generates such a group, is the task T-OP1-P2. Compared with Moretti, Theorem 142, p. 83 (read): (a) there is a unique self-adjoint generator A with U(t) = exp(-itA), (b) A psi = i lim (U(t) - 1) psi / t on the vectors where the limit exists; also with Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics (AMS online edition), Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, pp. 123-124 (read). The Hall chapters are cited but were not read. Difference to be approved by a maintainer (convention): the library's generator is -i d/dt U(t) at 0, with U(t) = exp(itA), the negative of Moretti's (U(t) = exp(-itA)).
- **LL-0164.** On a complex Hilbert space, a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group is determined by its generator: if U and V have the same generator then U(t) = V(t) for all t. This is the uniqueness part of Stone's theorem. Compared with Moretti, Theorem 142, p. 83 (read): (a) there is a unique self-adjoint generator A with U(t) = exp(-itA), (b) A psi = i lim (U(t) - 1) psi / t on the vectors where the limit exists; also with Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics (AMS online edition), Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, pp. 123-124 (read). The Hall chapters are cited but were not read. Difference to be approved by a maintainer (convention): the library's generator is -i d/dt U(t) at 0, with U(t) = exp(itA), the negative of Moretti's (U(t) = exp(-itA)).
- **LL-0165.** For the translation group (U(t) psi)(x) = psi(x + t) on L^2(R) and psi in the domain of its generator, there are smooth compactly supported functions psi_n with psi_n -> psi and psi_n' -> i A psi in L^2, where A is the generator: C_c^infinity is a core, and the generator is the momentum operator -i d/dx. The comparison with the cited source is pending: the registry location is the chapter, and the statement was not read there. Difference to be approved by a maintainer: the core property is stated through approximating sequences, not as the equality of the closure of the restriction with the generator.
- **LL-0166.** The operator -i d/dx on the C^2 functions supported inside (0, 1) is densely defined in L^2(0, 1), and its deficiency spaces at i and -i are one-dimensional, so it has self-adjoint extensions and none is distinguished. The comparison with the cited source is pending: the registry location is the chapter, and the statement was not read there. Difference to be approved by a maintainer: the domain is the C^2 functions supported inside (0, 1); the closure of the operator is the same from C_c^infinity (the closure of the momentum graph on the interval).
- **LL-0167.** In L^2(0, 1) x L^2(0, 1), the closure of the graph of -i d/dx on C_c^infinity(0, 1) equals the closure of its graph on the C^2 functions supported inside (0, 1). The proof mollifies. The comparison with the cited source is pending: the registry location is the chapter, and the statement was not read there.
- **LL-0168.** For a complex inner product space h, fockRepOf h is a Fock representation: Weyl unitaries W(f) satisfying the Weyl relations, with a unit vector Omega that is cyclic for them and has <Omega, W(f) Omega> = exp(-|f|^2 / 4). The Hilbert space is the reproducing kernel Hilbert space of the Fock kernel (Mathlib's RKHS.OfKernel). The representation difference is approved by the maintainers (18 November 2026): a Fock representation is characterised by its cyclic vacuum and vacuum expectation, not built on the symmetric Fock space; any two such representations are unitarily equivalent (uniqueness of the Fock representation). The comparison with the cited source is pending: the registry location is the chapter, and the statement was not read there.
- **LL-0169.** For two Fock representations R on K1 and S on K2 (complete) of the same complex inner product space, the unitary fockUnitary R S from K1 onto K2 maps the vacuum to the vacuum and intertwines the Weyl unitaries. The map W(f) Omega to W(f) Omega' is well defined and norm preserving on the dense span of these vectors and extends to a unitary. The representation difference of the existence of a Fock representation is approved by the maintainers (18 November 2026). The comparison with the cited source is pending: the registry location is the chapter, and the statement was not read there.
- **LL-0183.** On Matrix n n C with tau^{-i beta}(B) = e^{beta H} B e^{-beta H}: a matrix rho of trace 1 satisfies tr(rho A B) = tr(rho tau^{-i beta}(B) A) for all A, B (the beta-KMS condition, eq. (2.24)) iff rho = e^{-beta H} / tr e^{-beta H}. Compared with Jaksic-Ogata-Pautrat-Pillet, Section 2.9, eq. (2.24) and Proposition 2.20, p. 53 (read). The statement is more general than the source's: H is any matrix with tr e^{-beta H} != 0 (the source takes H self-adjoint, where this holds), and rho is only required to have trace 1 (the source's states are positive).
- **LL-0184.** For the momentum P = -i d/dx on L^2(0, 1): the domain of the adjoint is D_max, the functions absolutely continuous on [0, 1] with derivative in L^2 (mem_adjoint_iff_ac, in MomentumBoundary.lean); the closed operator P is the adjoint on D_0 = {psi in D_max : psi(0) = psi(1) = 0} and equals the closure of -i d/dx on the C^2 functions supported inside (0, 1) (momentumZero_eq_closure); a self-adjoint operator B extends P iff B = P_theta, the adjoint on D_theta = {psi in D_max : psi(1) = e^{i theta} psi(0)}, for some real theta. Compared with Bonneau-Faraut-Valent, Section 5.3, eq. (14), p. 8, and Appendix A.3, p. 19 (read). Differences, kind convention, to be approved by a maintainer: (a) the interval is [0, 1] (L = 1); (b) theta ranges over the reals instead of [0, 2 pi] (the same operators).

Here the quotient V = U⁻¹U' commutes with every field φ(w); it maps the vacuum to a vector killed by every annihilator, i.e. to a multiple c Ω₀ of the vacuum, and the closed subspace {x | V x = c x} is invariant under all fields, hence everything by the irreducibility of the Fock representation; |c| = 1 because V is isometric. The explicit formula (57) of Theorem 31 (3) is not formalised.
- **LL-0402.** Comparison pending (no source for the fermionic Wick theorem was read). Here A = ⊕ Mₙᵢ(ℝ): π extends to the complex-linear σ(x) = π(Re x) + i π(Im x) of ⊕ Mₙᵢ(ℂ), J is a real structure for it, and the uniqueness theorem for complex summands gives the unitary. - **LL-0255.** Compared with Krajewski, arXiv:hep-th/9701081, Section 3.1, p. 10 (read): 'all our formulae remain valid, provided the indices i and j label irreducible representations of A'. The complexification is an input; for A = ⊕ Mₙᵢ(ℝ) it is constructed in RealSummands.lean.

- **LL-0257.** Compared with Krajewski, arXiv:hep-th/9701081, Section 3.1, p. 10 (read): 'Mₙ(ℂ) has two inequivalent irreducible representations, the fundamental one and its complex conjugate. However, all our formulae remain valid, provided the indices i and j label irreducible representations of A'. Here A = ⊕ Mₙᵢ(ℂ) with a real-linear π: Q± = (1 ∓ i π(i·1))/2 split H into the parts where π is complex-linear (fundamental) and antilinear (conjugate); the units Q± π(E^i_αβ) of the blocks (i, ±) that occur (Q± π(1ᵢ) ≠ 0) and φ(a) = (aᵢ, āᵢ) give the complexification. The index set of the model is the set of representations (i, ±) that occur. Mixed algebras and the sign conditions of Table 1, p. 14 are not covered.
- **LL-0260.** Compared with Krajewski, arXiv:hep-th/9701081, Section 2, p. 2 (A = ⊕ Mₙᵢ(K), K = ℝ, ℂ, ℍ) and Section 3.1, p. 10 (read): 'Mₙ(ℝ) and Mₙ(ℍ) have only one irreducible representation, the fundamental one, whereas Mₙ(ℂ) has two inequivalent irreducible representations, the fundamental one and its complex conjugate. However, all our formulae remain valid, provided the indices i and j label irreducible representations of A'. Here A = ⊕ Mₙ(ℝ) × ⊕ Mₙ(ℂ) × ⊕ Mₙ(ℍ) with a real-linear π: the restrictions of π to the three factors give units ψ₁(E^i_αβ), ψ±(E^i_αβ) (ψ±(Y) = ½(ψ₂(Y) ∓ i ψ₂(iY)), over the representations (i, ±) that occur) and the quaternionic units of M₂ₙ(ℂ); together they are one system of matrix units, and the uniqueness theorem for complex summands gives the unitary onto the model indexed by the irreducible representations that occur. The sign conditions of Table 1, p. 14 (the S⁰-real structure and the intersection form) are not covered.
- **LL-0262.** Compared with Krajewski, arXiv:hep-th/9701081, Section 3.3, p. 13 (read): 'Since χ = Σ_p π(x^p) J π(y^p) J⁻¹, with x^p, y^p ∈ A, χᵢⱼ is scalar matrix. Furthermore χᵢⱼ = ±1 as follows from χ² = 1. We also have [χ, J] = 0 so that χᵢⱼ = χⱼᵢ.' Here for a complex-linear triple over ⊕ Mₙᵢ(ℂ) and an orientable grading γ = Σ_p π(x_p) J π(y_p) J: γ acts on the multiplicity space Vᵢⱼ as cᵢⱼ = Σ_p (x_p)ᵢ₀₀ conj((y_p)ⱼ₀₀), cᵢⱼ = ±1 on a nonzero vertex and cⱼᵢ = cᵢⱼ.
- **LL-0263.** Compared with Krajewski, arXiv:hep-th/9701081, Section 3.3, p. 14 and Table 1 (read): 'In the real case, it is still given by a symmetric matrix with entries in Z whose indices label irreducibles representations of A. However, it is no longer the intersection form and the signs of its entries satisfy additional requirements that are summarized ... in table 1': μ_{iαj} μ_{iᾱj} ≥ 0 and μ_{iαjβ} μ_{iᾱjβ̄} ≥ 0. Here μ_kl = Re(c_kl) r_kl on the complexified model of a mixed algebra ⊕ Mₙ(ℝ) × ⊕ Mₙ(ℂ) × ⊕ Mₙ(ℍ) with an orientable grading; the conditions are stated for both representations of a complex summand that occur. The intersection form ∩ᵢⱼ = Tr(χ π(pᵢ) J π(pⱼ) J⁻¹) of minimal projections pᵢ, pⱼ is every entry of Table 1: μ, Σ_α μ, 2μ (real against real, complex, quaternionic), Σ_αβ μ, 2 Σ_α μ (complex against complex, quaternionic) and 4μ (quaternionic against quaternionic), where μ_kl = c_kl r_kl with c_kl the scalar of the chirality on the vertex.
- **LL-0372.** The converse of LL-0219. Krajewski, arXiv:hep-th/9701081, Section 3.4, p. 15 (read), states that the Dirac operator is given by D = Delta + J Delta J^-1 with Delta hermitian, commuting with J pi(A) J^-1 and anticommuting with chi. Here, for a real graded finite spectral triple of KO-dimension 0 and a hermitian Delta commuting with J pi(b) J and anticommuting with the grading, D' = Delta + J Delta J is self-adjoint, satisfies the first-order condition and D J = J D, and anticommutes with the grading, so the same representation, J and grading form a real graded triple with Dirac operator D'. Together with LL-0219 (every Dirac operator has this form, with Delta unique) this is the statement of the section in the case where the chirality is a scalar on each vertex. The paper's own proof was not compared line by line; the first-order condition is proved here from order zero and the commutation of Delta with J pi(b) J.

- **LL-0268.** Compared with Abdesselam and Rivasseau, arXiv:hep-th/9409094, Theorem III.1, eq. (III.2), p. 13, and the definition of h^F_l on p. 3 (read): for H in the space of smooth functions from R^{P_n} to a Banach space V, H(1) is the sum over the forests F of the integrals over the h_l in the unit interval, l in F, of the product over l in F of the partial derivatives in x_l of H at X^F(h), whose entry at the link l is the infimum of the h along the unique path of F joining the ends of l, and 0 if there is none. forest_formula_restrict is this statement for H : (Link n -> R) -> V with ContDiff R infinity H and V a real Banach space; forest_formula states it with the integral over the whole cube of R^{P_n} of the same integrand, a function of the h_l, l in F, only. Differences from the cited theorem, all representation, with the meaning unchanged: the points 1, ..., n are Fin n and P_n is Link n, the unordered pairs s(a, b) with a /= b; X^F(h)_l is defined by the ultrametric of F (the largest h_m, m in F, such that the ends of l are joined by the links of F with parameter at least h_m, 0 if none), which for h >= 0, in particular on the unit cube, is the infimum along the path of F and 0 if there is no path (forestPoint_eq_path_inf, forestPoint_of_not_linked); the integral over the unit cube of F is the integral over F -> R for the product of the uniform measures on the unit interval, h extended by 0 off F, which does not change X^F(h) (forestPoint_congr); the product of the partial derivatives is the iterated Frechet partial derivative pdF along the coordinate vectors, independent of the order (pd_comm, pdF_insert). Proof: not the source's (the algebraic formula (II.1) for polynomials and density in S, pp. 13-14), but the iterated Taylor interpolation of Gurau, Rivasseau and Sfondrini, arXiv:1401.5003, Theorem 6.1, eq. (6.1), p. 107, and its proof, pp. 107-109 (read), as an induction on the number of links in which the new link is the one with the smallest parameter (T_succ, interp_insert_update); ties have measure zero (cube_eq_null).

Difference, representation, with the meaning unchanged: positive is Matrix.PosSemidef (symmetric with x^T X x >= 0); the matrix can be singular (one link with parameter 1 gives the 2 x 2 matrix of ones), so the source's positive is positive semidefinite. Not a difference: the statement holds for any finite set of links and needs only w_l <= 1 on F, which contains the source's case of a forest with parameters in the unit interval. Notes:

- **LL-0345.** Part of QU3, which stays open. For a field k and a unit q, the k-algebra on generators E, F, K, K⁻¹ with K K⁻¹ = K⁻¹ K = 1, K E = q² E K, K F = q⁻² F K and (q − q⁻¹)(E F − F E) = K − K⁻¹ carries a Hopf algebra structure with Δ E = E ⊗ K + 1 ⊗ E, Δ F = F ⊗ 1 + K⁻¹ ⊗ F, Δ K = K ⊗ K, ε E = ε F = 0, ε K = 1, S E = −E K⁻¹, S F = −K F, S K = K⁻¹. These are the common conventions; matching them to the normalisation of the cited chapter was not checked, since the chapter was not read at that location. The commutation relation is written without division, so it is defined for every q; for q² = 1 it is a different (non-quantum) algebra. No representation theory, R-matrix, ribbon element or modular category is proved here (QU3 stays open); the checks in UqSl2Tests.lean are identities on generators.
- **LL-0346.** Part of QU3 (G3-200), which stays open. The matrices satisfy the five defining relations of UqSl2 (K K⁻¹ = K⁻¹ K = 1, K E = q² E K, K F = q⁻² F K, (q − q⁻¹)(E F − F E) = K − K⁻¹), so they define an algebra homomorphism fundRep by the universal property of the quotient (fundGen_rel). No hypothesis on q: it also holds at roots of unity and at q² = 1. The comparison with Turaev, Chapter XI, is pending: the book was not read at the cited location.
- **LL-0347.** Part of QU3 (G3-200), which stays open. The tensor square fundTensorRep is the representation on k² ⊗ k² with E, F, K, K⁻¹ acting by the matrices fundCoE, fundCoF, fundCoK, fundCoKi of ΔE = E ⊗ K + 1 ⊗ E, ΔF = F ⊗ 1 + K⁻¹ ⊗ F, ΔK = K ⊗ K, ΔK⁻¹ = K⁻¹ ⊗ K⁻¹ (the coproduct of UqSl2); it is shown to be a representation by the defining relations (tensorGen_rel). Ř = P R is the unique intertwiner up to the identity with the eigenvalue q on v₀₀, v₁₁ and trace q − q⁻¹ on the weight-zero space, so it is the R-matrix of this representation in the form Ř. Not proved: that the universal R-matrix exists and acts as Ř, and that fundTensorRep is the tensor product of fundRep with itself through the library's comul (the matrices were checked against comul_E, comul_F, comul_K by reading, not by a Lean statement). The braid relation holds for every unit q; the Hecke relation is a quadratic relation with eigenvalues q and −q⁻¹. The comparison with Turaev, Chapter XI, is pending.

- **LL-0348.** GC4 (G3-132). Flat phase space X × X with Physlib's Poisson bracket; the Dirac bracket {f,g} − Σ {f,φ_a} (C⁻¹)_ab {φ_b,g} is antisymmetric and vanishes against a constraint when C is invertible. The circle particle and the wrong-count check are circle_isSecondClass and circle_wrong_count (Lightlike/Tests/Constraints.lean). finrank_reducedTangent: dim of the reduced tangent space is dim E − 2 dim(orbit), for a linear action at a zero of the moment map. The comparison with the cited sources is pending in the registry (Wipf hep-th/9312078 is not a registered source; the comparison note docs/notes/gc4-source-dirac.md is the record).
- **LL-0349.** GC4 (G3-132). Termination by counting under linear independence of the gradients (regularity is a hypothesis; the smooth existence of the secondary constraints is not proved here). Without regularity there is no termination: the chain {x ≤ 1/(k+1)} in ℝ (DiracNonlinear.lean). The comparison with the cited sources is pending in the registry (Wipf hep-th/9312078 is not a registered source; the comparison note docs/notes/gc4-source-dirac.md is the record).
- **LL-0350.** GC4 (G3-132). Hypotheses: the bracket is first order (br f g x = B x (df) (dg)) and the stages are regular. Equivalent to the left-null-vector form of the consistency condition (chiFun_zero_iff_leftNull; Wipf hep-th/9312078, Sec. 3.3, pp. 16-17). ## Stated targets

Statements defined in Lean and checked to be well-formed, whose proofs are open. They are not results.

| ID | Target | Area | Tier | Lean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LL-0313 | Wigner's classification of irreducible, strongly continuous, unitary, positive-energy representations of the Poincaré group, stated as a precise proposition with a non-vacuity check (see note) | SL(2,ℂ) and its unitary principal series | established | `Lightlike.Lorentz.Poincare.WignerClassification`, `Lightlike.Lorentz.Poincare.trivialRep_classified` in [ClassificationStatement.lean](../Lightlike/Lorentz/PoincareIrreps/ClassificationStatement.lean) |

Notes:

- **LL-0313.** HA6 (G1-055), the lockable statement of the milestone. WignerClassification is a Prop, NOT proved: every such representation is trivial on the translations, or equivalent to a massive poincareRep, or to a massless finite-helicity lightPoincareRep, or massless of infinite spin (MasslessNotHelicity). Its proof needs Mackey's imprimitivity theorem; isSystemOfImprimitivity_inducedL2 (Imprimitivity.lean) is one ingredient. Non-vacuity: trivialRep_classified (the trivial representation falls in the first case). The statement uses the library's own definitions of equivalence and positive energy; comparison with Weinberg and Wigner pending (not read). Compared with Wigner, Ann. Math. 40 (1939) 149-204, Section 7B, p. 198, The final result (read): the classes P_+^j (P > 0, j = n/2: EquivMassive with P = m²), 0_+^s (s = h/2, an integer or half-integer of either sign or zero: EquivMassless) and 0_+(Xi), 0'_+(Xi) (continuous spin, Xi > 0, single or double valued: MasslessNotHelicity) are the positive-energy classes; the class 0_0 (every translation trivial) and the class P < 0 are 'not determined' there; the negative-energy classes P_-, 0_- and the space-like class are excluded here by positive energy. The first case of the statement is Wigner's 0_0. Differences: (1) the continuous-spin classes are given only negatively (not a helicity representation), so for the massless part the statement says only that the spectrum lies in the light cone; (2) only completeness is stated: that each listed representation is irreducible is LL-0310 and LL-0311, and that different parameters give inequivalent representations is not stated; (3) Weinberg, QFT I, Section 2.5, was not read: that comparison is pending.
